a83.speaker: State Department
a83.name: State Department
a83.speech: referred to them as "certain abortifacient birth control commodities from terminated Biden-era USAID contracts."

a83.speaker: Belgian foreign ministry
a83.name: Belgian foreign ministry
a83.speech: Is seeking alternatives to destroying the contraceptives.

a83.speaker: Jeanne Shaheen, US Senator
a83.name: Jeanne Shaheen
a83.title: US Senator
a83.speech: Is working on legislation to prevent the destruction, highlighting the urgent global need for these supplies.

a83.speaker: Humanitarian groups like Doctors Without Borders (MSF)
a83.name: Humanitarian groups like Doctors Without Borders (MSF)
a83.speech: warn of severe contraceptive shortages in vulnerable regions.

a83.speaker: The Lancet (medical journal)
a83.name: The Lancet (medical journal)
a83.speech: Estimates significant mortality increases from USAID funding cuts.

a101.speaker: Political analysts and citizens
a101.name: Political analysts and citizens
a101.speech: Have expressed outrage at Chimombo's actions, arguing that they undermine the very essence of Bingu's legacy.

a101.speaker: A prominent political commentator (anonymous)
a101.name: A prominent political commentator (anonymous)
a101.speech: "If Bingu were alive today, he would not have allowed his name to be politically exploited in this manner" ; "We must protect his legacy from those who seek to tarnish it for their own ambitions."

a359.speaker: Steenkamp, Namibian education ministry official
a359.name: Steenkamp
a359.title: Namibian education ministry official
a359.speech: Said the option of a verification-of-identity form is only available to full-time candidates, adding that all other candidates must be in possession of acceptable identification documents to enter exam venues — an original national identity document, a valid original passport, a valid original driver's licence, an original voter card, or a learner card issued by schools to full-time candidates; noted that identification will only be accepted if it shows the candidate's name, date of birth or identity number, and a recent photograph.

a359.speaker: Steenkamp, Namibian education ministry official
a359.name: Steenkamp
a359.title: Namibian education ministry official
a359.speech: Reiterated that full-time learners without national documents will be allowed to sit for their exams as the ministry will also accept the verification-of-identity form; stressed that, as per a circular issued, candidates qualifying to use this form must follow the procedures before the exams start — obtaining a recent passport photo certified as valid by the school principal, completing the form in the presence of the principal and attaching the photo in the space provided. She urged principals and tuition centres to convey this information to candidates in good time to enable them to obtain their identity documents or forms before the commencement of exams.

a359.speaker: Namibian Sun (newspaper report)
a359.name: Namibian Sun (newspaper report)
a359.speech: Reported yesterday that learners without national documents — thought to be in their thousands across the country — will not be allowed to sit for the Namibia Senior Secondary Certificate Ordinary Level (NSSCO) grade 11 and Advanced Subsidiary (AS) level grade 12 exams in November.

a401.speaker: Patriotic Front (PF), Zambian opposition party
a401.name: Patriotic Front (PF)
a401.title: Zambian opposition party
a401.speech: Has called on government to ensure that the 2009 budget was designed in a manner that would address the country's challenges which have come as a result of global economic recession.

a401.speaker: Guy Scott, PF vice president
a401.name: Guy Scott
a401.title: PF vice president
a401.speech: Said the opposition party is concerned with the negative impact of the global financial crisis; speaking during a media briefing at the party headquarters in Lusaka, said there was need for government to heed to calls from his party to cut on its expenditure ; said cutting government expenditure would help address some of the challenges the country is facing due to the prevailing global financial meltdown.

a401.speaker: Guy Scott, PF vice president
a401.name: Guy Scott
a401.title: PF vice president
a401.speech: Urged government to expeditiously issue a report on the alleged secret Central Intelligence Agency (CIA) prisons in the country as reported in the international media ; said his party was waiting for a report from government because the American government through its embassy in the country has since denied operating secret CIA prisons in Zambia.

a401.speaker: American government, through its embassy in Zambia
a401.name: American government
a401.title: through its embassy in Zambia
a401.speech: Has since denied operating secret CIA prisons in Zambia.

a401.speaker: Given Lubinda, PF spokesperson
a401.name: Given Lubinda
a401.title: PF spokesperson
a401.speech: Alleged that most of the Permanent Secretaries which were recently appointed to government were not competent to run the civil service because they did not have the technical knowledge and experience ; charged that the appointments amounted to abuse of office and a campaign strategy by the ruling party for the 2011 elections ; further alleged that most of those appointed to the position of permanent secretaries are people that campaigned for President Banda during the October 30th 2008 presidential elections.

a401.speaker: Kuyoto Kunyanda and William Harrington, former MMD officials and ministers in the second republic
a401.name: Kuyoto Kunyanda and William Harrington
a401.title: former MMD officials and ministers in the second republic
a401.speech: Announced their resignation from the ruling MMD to join opposition PF at the same media briefing, citing weaknesses in the MMD leadership.

a493.speaker: Foster Mohale, South African health department spokesperson
a493.name: Foster Mohale
a493.title: South African health department spokesperson
a493.speech: Says South Africa has accepted an offer of just over $29 million (about R520 million) from the Global Fund to Fight Aids, TB and Malaria to buy the twice-a-year anti-HIV jab, lenacapavir, that research shows could help to end Aids in the country.

a493.speaker: Boitumelo Semete-Makokotlela, chief executive of the South African Health Products Regulatory Authority (Sahpra)
a493.name: Boitumelo Semete-Makokotlela
a493.title: chief executive of the South African Health Products Regulatory Authority (Sahpra)
a493.speech: Told Bhekisisa it is aiming to have lenacapavir registered in South Africa before the end of the year.

a493.speaker: Khadija Jamaloodien, South African health department's head of procurement
a493.name: Khadija Jamaloodien
a493.title: South African health department's head of procurement
a493.speech: Said the lenacapavir funds from the Global Fund will become available in October, when the roll-out period of South Africa's next grant, known as Grant Cycle 7, kicks in ; confirmed that the health department did receive the Global Fund letter, and says South Africa's letter instructs the country to submit its first order, for planning purposes, by 30 September under an "agreed procurement mechanism."

a493.speaker: Khadija Jamaloodien, South African health department's head of procurement
a493.name: Khadija Jamaloodien
a493.title: South African health department's head of procurement
a493.speech: Cautions further discussions with the Global Fund and Gilead will be needed about the governance around the pricing of the product ; "We have a transparent pricing system, guided by the Public Finance Management Act. Even if we procure medicine with Global Fund money, we have to follow the same rules that the treasury requires us to follow with tenders, which includes revealing the price at which the medicine is bought."

a493.speaker: Two studies released last year
a493.name: Two studies released last year
a493.speech: Showed the medicine completely protects young women from contracting the virus and works almost as well for men, transgender and gender-nonbinary people.

a493.speaker: Modelling study
a493.name: Modelling study
a493.speech: Shows that if between two and four million HIV-negative people in South Africa use the jab every year over the next eight years, the medication could end Aids as a public health threat by 2032.

a493.speaker: Joint United Nations Programme on HIV and Aids (UNAids) report
a493.name: Joint United Nations Programme on HIV and Aids (UNAids) report
a493.speech: 170 000 people got newly infected with HIV in 2024, while there were 53 000 Aids-related deaths.

a493.speaker: Scientists and policymakers
a493.name: Scientists and policymakers
a493.speech: Say the Global Fund money for South Africa is not nearly enough to put two to four million people a year in South Africa on the lenacapavir jab — and even if it was, the country's health system won't be able to roll the medicine out that fast.

a493.speaker: Global Fund (announcement of July 9)
a493.name: Global Fund (announcement of July 9)
a493.speech: Announced that it has the "ambition" to finance enough lenacapavir for two million HIV-negative people — in the low- and middle-income countries it supports — over the next three years.

a493.speaker: Some activists
a493.name: Some activists
a493.speech: Say it's still possible for the US administration to come on board with paying to roll out lenacapavir.

a493.speaker: Mitchell Warren, executive director of Avac
a493.name: Mitchell Warren
a493.title: executive director of Avac
a493.speech: "We now stand at a moment of reckoning and a moment of choice" ; "While a lot of the choices over the last six months have been made by an American politician [Donald Trump] who doesn't care about the pandemic or science generally, our choice is to make decisions based on the science that we all now know. Which is that lenacapavir is our most potent opportunity."

a493.speaker: Global Fund letter sent in early July to the nine early roll-out countries
a493.name: Global Fund letter sent in early July to the nine early roll-out countries
a493.speech: Asked the governments to budget for $60 (about R1 076) per patient a year ($30, or R576, per six-monthly dose), to buy lenacapavir ; makes it clear that the amount "reflects the country contribution only, to be used for budgeting purposes, and should not be considered the product price" ; states that the gap between the price that the fund pays Gilead per patient a year and the $60 that countries will pay for with their Global Fund grants will be covered by private sector funding.

a493.speaker: Hui Yang, the Global Fund's head of supply operations
a493.name: Hui Yang
a493.title: the Global Fund's head of supply operations
a493.speech: Confirmed to Bhekisisa that the gap will be paid for by a $150 million (about R2.68 billion) donation of the UK-based Children's Investment Fund Foundation to the Global Fund.

a493.speaker: Gilead Sciences
a493.name: Gilead Sciences
a493.speech: Said it will have a "not-for-profit" price for low- and middle-income countries such as South Africa, such as the one they negotiated with the Global Fund, but isn't allowing the fund to make it public ; argues that because the not-for-profit price is based on the actual cost of making lenacapavir, and shipping it to countries, it can't declare that cost.

a493.speaker: Several scientists and activists at the HIV science conference
a493.name: Several scientists and activists at the HIV science conference
a493.speech: Told Bhekisisa the rumoured not-for-profit price that Gilead has negotiated with the Global Fund is $100 per person a year.

a493.speaker: Avac (analysis of events)
a493.name: Avac (analysis of events)
a493.speech: Confirms that the rumoured not-for-profit price is $100 per person a year ; has identified 16 top lenacapavir markets, of which South Africa is — by far — the largest because of the country's high number of new HIV infections.

a493.speaker: Gilead and the Global Fund
a493.name: Gilead and the Global Fund
a493.speech: Neither has confirmed the $100 per person a year amount.

a493.speaker: Caroline Almeida, Gilead's head of public affairs
a493.name: Caroline Almeida
a493.title: Gilead's head of public affairs
a493.speech: "Gilead doesn't publicly disclose manufacturing costs for any of our medications," told Bhekisisa in Kigali.

a493.speaker: Health Justice Initiative and other activist groups (press release)
a493.name: Health Justice Initiative and other activist groups (press release)
a493.speech: "Gilead's secrecy will obstruct civil society activism for lower drug prices and keep prices high in middle-income countries [such as South Africa] where Gilead negotiates prices directly" ; "Such secrecy undermines the power of buyers to negotiate affordable prices and violates the human rights of all people to access information and lifesaving tools."

a493.speaker: Research released by Wits RHI in Kigali
a493.name: Research released by Wits RHI in Kigali
a493.speech: Shows South Africans are open to using the jab: 56% of just over 1 700 participants in a survey in Tshwane, Mthatha and Gqeberha, who were already using public sector HIV prevention services, said they would take a lenacapavir shot.

a493.speaker: Mitchell Warren, executive director of Avac
a493.name: Mitchell Warren
a493.title: executive director of Avac
a493.speech: "Pricing transparency has been a long-standing challenge, as companies try to balance their commercial pricing and marketing strategies with their global public health strategies. We clearly need a new model or compact for pricing that helps break the cycle of small thinking and limited impact."

a659.speaker: Nthoateng Lebona, Principal Secretary of the Lesotho Finance Ministry
a659.name: Nthoateng Lebona
a659.title: Principal Secretary of the Lesotho Finance Ministry
a659.speech: Noted during the virtual launch of the African Economic Outlook 2025 Country Focus Report for Lesotho that government is investing in skills development for young people through Technical and Vocational Education Training (TVET) to close the skills mismatch and produce employable, job-ready youth ; mentioned that, aligning with the theme, it is befitting to look at capital not in the narrow sense, but human, natural, financial capital and technological advancement.

a659.speaker: Nthoateng Lebona, Principal Secretary of the Lesotho Finance Ministry
a659.name: Nthoateng Lebona
a659.title: Principal Secretary of the Lesotho Finance Ministry
a659.speech: Said the challenges have been exacerbated by the recent developments of a shift in global trade policies and the abrupt slash of foreign aid, and that these shocks have had "profound effects on our economy and people, increasing the cost of living, constraining the fiscal space, disrupting trade flows and increasing the cost of capital."

a659.speaker: Nthoateng Lebona, Principal Secretary of the Lesotho Finance Ministry
a659.name: Nthoateng Lebona
a659.title: Principal Secretary of the Lesotho Finance Ministry
a659.speech: Said Lesotho, like many African nations, is blessed with natural endowments: "our high quality diamonds and abundant water resources support our economy and generate revenue through exports and royalties. Yet these blessings, while significant, are finite, therefore they must be utilised in the manner that translates into the equivalents productivity." ; said that beyond natural resources Lesotho recognises the transformative potential of its renewable energy landscape, particularly hydropower and wind energy, and that harnessing this potential is not only a national imperative but also a regional opportunity, positioning Lesotho to contribute meaningfully to regional energy security and climate-friendly development as Africa advances toward a green economy.

a659.speaker: Nthoateng Lebona, Principal Secretary of the Lesotho Finance Ministry
a659.name: Nthoateng Lebona
a659.title: Principal Secretary of the Lesotho Finance Ministry
a659.speech: Said Lesotho's macroeconomic outlook is increasingly precarious due to recent shocks, noted that the fiscal position is projected to remain stable in 2024/25, and continued that government will allocate more resources to investment spending, underscoring its commitment to infrastructure and economic transformation in the short to medium term: "The economy recorded modest growth of 2.5 percent in 2024/25 and is projected to progress to 3.4 percent in 2025/26, mainly driven by the construction sector. We need to close the productivity gap and move to higher value addition, implement at accelerated pace the investment climate reforms, economic and market diversification. Make use of digital technology in agriculture, manufacturing, education, e-government, e-health, and integrate into international markets." ; concluded by stating that the need for a multi-pronged approach and increased financing to invest at scale and in the right sectors, while dealing with threats of global shocks and climate change to accelerate Lesotho's growth, is well noted.

a659.speaker: African Economic Outlook 2025 Country Focus Report for Lesotho (African Development Bank Group)
a659.name: African Economic Outlook 2025 Country Focus Report for Lesotho (African Development Bank Group)
a659.speech: According to the report, Lesotho's economy grew modestly at 2.4 percent in 2024 driven by infrastructure projects like the Lesotho Highlands Water Project Phase II, inflation eased to six percent and the fiscal balance recorded a surplus of 8.4 percent of GDP; growth is projected to slow to 1.1 percent in 2025 and 0.5 percent in 2026, with fiscal and external balances expected to weaken as SACU revenues decline, Official Development Assistance (ODA) shrinks, and capital spending rises. Key risks include climate vulnerabilities, sluggish growth in key trading partners, escalating trade tensions, ODA cuts and the aftermath of the cancellation of the Millennium Challenge Corporation Compact II (MCC II). The report recommends economic diversification, expanded trade partnerships, stronger institutional quality and governance, and reforms to enhance transparency, accountability and fiscal discipline: "Encouraging private sector participation through regulatory reform will attract investment, foster innovation, improve service delivery and reduce the fiscal burden on the government, driving sustainable economic growth."

a659.speaker: Government of Lesotho / Officials (unnamed)
a659.name: Government of Lesotho / Officials (unnamed)
a659.speech: Emphasized the importance of investing in skills development for young people, highlighting that a skilled youth population is essential for national development and attracting investment, and called for collaboration with educational institutions and private stakeholders to achieve this vision.

a748.speaker: United Nations Population Fund (UNFPA), through the "Safe Birth Africa" project
a748.name: United Nations Population Fund (UNFPA)
a748.title: through the "Safe Birth Africa" project
a748.speech: Holds that no woman should lose her life while giving life.

a748.speaker: Diene Keita, Executive Director of UNFPA
a748.name: Diene Keita
a748.title: Executive Director of UNFPA
a748.speech: Said the gesture goes well beyond a simple handover of medicines, that it embodies a collective promise: to do everything possible so that every Ivorian woman has access to quality care allowing her to give birth safely; and that her organisation reaffirms its determination to support the government and all its partners in building policies and programmes guaranteeing universal access to safe, equitable and quality maternal health services. "Together, let us continue our efforts to build a future in which motherhood will never again be synonymous with danger, but will remain what it must be: a moment of life, joy and fulfilment."

a748.speaker: Charles Aka Koffi, Chief of Staff of the Minister of Health, Public Hygiene and Universal Health Coverage of Côte d'Ivoire
a748.name: Charles Aka Koffi
a748.title: Chief of Staff of the Minister of Health, Public Hygiene and Universal Health Coverage of Côte d'Ivoire
a748.speech: Welcomed the implementation of the Safe Birth Africa project: "Thanks to this investment, access to health services for pregnant women will be markedly improved, particularly in the Gbeke and Gontougo regions, and, on the other hand, the infrastructure and skills of health personnel will be strengthened." ; "The Safe Birth Africa project will be an opportunity for Côte d'Ivoire to further consolidate its gains in maternal and child health."

a748.speaker: Charles Aka Koffi, Chief of Staff of the Minister of Health, Public Hygiene and Universal Health Coverage of Côte d'Ivoire
a748.name: Charles Aka Koffi
a748.title: Chief of Staff of the Minister of Health, Public Hygiene and Universal Health Coverage of Côte d'Ivoire
a748.speech: Hailed the inclusion of reproductive health among development priorities and the support of the African Development Bank (AfDB), which aims to strengthen reproductive health services, including family planning, maternal and child care, and the fight against sexually transmitted diseases, with the aim of improving quality of life in Africa.

a748.speaker: Clarisse Kayo Mahi, Chair of the Board of Directors of the New Public Health Pharmacy of Côte d'Ivoire (NPSP-CI)
a748.name: Clarisse Kayo Mahi
a748.title: Chair of the Board of Directors of the New Public Health Pharmacy of Côte d'Ivoire (NPSP-CI)
a748.speech: Stated that the gesture highlights the fruitful partnership between Côte d'Ivoire and UNFPA, supported by the AfDB, recalling that since 2014 the partnership between NPSP-CI and UNFPA has made it possible to manage, on behalf of the National Mother and Child Health Programme, at least 1 billion CFA francs of health products per year for reproductive health and family planning. "It is therefore a pleasure for me to welcome this partnership of more than ten years in the field of mother and child health, which will continue with the recent signing of the tripartite agreement between the Ministry of Health, UNFPA and NPSP-CI for a renewable period of 12 months."

a748.speaker: Irchad Ramiandrasoa Razaaly, Representative of the European Union in Côte d'Ivoire
a748.name: Irchad Ramiandrasoa Razaaly
a748.title: Representative of the European Union in Côte d'Ivoire
a748.speech: Reaffirmed the Union's commitment to strengthening the Ivorian health system to promote a better quality of life for all the women and young people of the country.

a776.speaker: Nigerian military high command
a776.name: Nigerian military high command
a776.speech: Provided an insight into what transpired between terrorists and personnel attached to the Forward Operating Base, Sabon Gari Area in Damboa Local Government Area of Borno State; confirmed that 6 soldiers lost their lives during the encounter while 34 terrorists, who had attempted to surprise the troops and retaliate the recent killing of their commander and combatants, were eliminated.

a776.speaker: Daily Trust (newspaper report)
a776.name: Daily Trust (newspaper report)
a776.speech: Had exclusively reported that four days after Boko Haram terrorists overran the military base, many soldiers were still unaccounted for.

a776.speaker: Stakeholders within the security circle
a776.name: Stakeholders within the security circle
a776.speech: Described the development of soldiers still being unaccounted for as "worrisome."

a776.speaker: Edward Buba, Major-General, Director of Defence Media Operations
a776.name: Edward Buba
a776.title: Major-General, Director of Defence Media Operations
a776.speech: Explained that most of the bodies recovered were those of the terrorists; disclosed that the terrorists were neutralised by the air component of Operation HADIN KAI which conducted air interdiction; said Battle Damage Assessment revealed that several terrorists were killed while their weapons were recovered, and that the Vigilante Commander got injured when he stepped on Improvised Explosive Devices (IEDs) but the troops reinforcement team's timely arrival saved the day ; "On 4 January 2025, an unspecified number of ISWAP/BHT terrorists riding on motorcycles and gun trucks engaged troops deployed in Sabon Gari Village of Damboa LGA of Borno State in a fire fight. The terrorists had attempted to surprise troops and retaliate the recent killing of their commander and combatants by troops. The terrorists were taken unaware, when troops fighting patrol returning to the Base foiled their planned attack as soon as the attack commenced. Additionally, troops reinforcement team comprised of elements of Civilian Joint Taskforce, vigilante as well as hybrid forces timely arrived the scene to overpower the terrorists. Furthermore, though troops reinforcement team encountered Improvise Explosive Device injuring the Vigilante Commander. The reinforcement team arrived timely to decimate the fleeing terrorist. Furthermore, the air component of Operation HADIN KAI conducted air interdiction on the fleeing terrorists. Battle Damage Assessment revealed several killed terrorists and recovered weapons. On the whole, 34 terrorist were killed and 23 AK 47 weapons recovered. Troops also recovered with over 200 rounds of 7.62mm special ammunitions. Sadly, 6 personnel were killed in action."

a776.speaker: Edward Buba, Major-General, Director of Defence Media Operations
a776.name: Edward Buba
a776.title: Major-General, Director of Defence Media Operations
a776.speech: Appealed to the media organisations and Nigerians to respect non-disclosure of the names of killed-in-action personnel to allow administrative procedures of notifying their Next of Kin.

a820.speaker: Ayaa Irene Lokang, Director of AMDISS
a820.name: Ayaa Irene Lokang
a820.title: Director of AMDISS
a820.speech: Says climate change is a global issue and all discussions now surround the issue of climate change and its impact on human beings and on wildlife: “The issue of climate change has become a global. All over the world people are discussing the issue of climate change and the associated impact on Human being and on Wildlife.” ; “We in South Sudan will not continue to keep quiet while seeing the dangers being created by the climate change. We have witness many cases of floods and droughts in different parts of South Sudan, all these are affecting us as a country.”

a820.speaker: Ayaa Irene Lokang, Director of AMDISS
a820.name: Ayaa Irene Lokang
a820.title: Director of AMDISS
a820.speech: “Media play crucial role in ensuring that Environmental issues are amplified. We look at Radio as one of the powerful tools in amplifying issues to do with Climate Change.”

a820.speaker: Jacob Atem, Representative of the Norwegian People’s Aid (NPA)
a820.name: Jacob Atem
a820.title: Representative of the Norwegian People’s Aid (NPA)
a820.speech: Pledged their continued support to the media and civil society in thematic areas: “We, as Norwegian People’s Aid (NPA), will continue to support the media and civil society despite the challenges caused by the cut of USAID funding.”

a922.speaker: Puntland State of Somalia (Cabinet appeal)
a922.name: Puntland State of Somalia (Cabinet appeal)
a922.speech: Has made an urgent appeal for humanitarian and stabilization assistance for residents affected by ongoing military operations targeting Islamic State (ISIS) militants in the remote mountains of the Bari region; the Cabinet meeting in Bosaso resulted in an urgent appeal to humanitarian aid groups and international partners involved in stabilization efforts.

a922.speaker: Puntland government reports
a922.name: Puntland government reports
a922.speech: According to government reports, over 19,640 families have been uprooted by the counter-terrorism operation, which was launched in late December under the codename “Operation Hillaac.”

a922.speaker: Abdi Farah Said, Puntland Interior Minister
a922.name: Abdi Farah Said
a922.title: Puntland Interior Minister
a922.speech: Called on United Nations agencies and other international partners to provide immediate assistance to displaced families and communities affected by the conflict: “We are particularly appealing to UN agencies to provide humanitarian aid to those affected by the ongoing operation. Additionally, we urge agencies involved in stabilization projects, such as USAID, to assist communities in the liberated areas” ; emphasized the need for essential services in the areas cleared of militants, including education, healthcare, water, and roads: “These services will enable displaced locals to resume their livelihoods and allow the government to ensure their safety once they return.”

a922.speaker: Ubah Abdirashid Mohamed Hirsi, Puntland’s Minister of Humanitarian Management
a922.name: Ubah Abdirashid Mohamed Hirsi
a922.title: Puntland’s Minister of Humanitarian Management
a922.speech: “So far, 19,640 families have fled their homes and are in desperate need of emergency support. Poor rainfall last year compounded the difficulties these families were already facing, and now this displacement has worsened their situation.”

a922.speaker: Mohamud Aideed Dirir, Puntland Minister of Information
a922.name: Mohamud Aideed Dirir
a922.title: Puntland Minister of Information
a922.speech: Praised the progress made by Puntland Security Forces (PSF), despite limited resources: “The counter-ISIS operation, which we initially projected to take months, has achieved remarkable success in just a few weeks. ISIS fighters are on the run, abandoning their positions, and Puntland forces are pursuing them in the remote mountains” ; commended local communities for their role in providing intelligence that has been instrumental in tracking the militants.

a971.speaker: World Bank
a971.name: World Bank
a971.speech: Financial inclusion as defined by the World Bank refers to the share of individuals and firms that use financial services such as transactions, payments, savings, credit and insurance.

a971.speaker: The African Banking Survey, 2016, a report by PwC
a971.name: The African Banking Survey
a971.title: 2016, a report by PwC
a971.speech: Pointed to the fact that bank CEOs’ priority is to secure and increase market share in the domestic regions.

a971.speaker: Likhit Wagle, a former PwC partner
a971.name: Likhit Wagle
a971.title: a former PwC partner
a971.speech: Quipped that ‘the real key problem in financial inclusion today is not so much in opening accounts-that’s happening fairly successfully-but we get stuck with the fact that these are very low balance accounts that are not very profitable’.

a1077.speaker: National Athletics Association of Zimbabwe (NAAZ)
a1077.name: National Athletics Association of Zimbabwe (NAAZ)
a1077.speech: Has declared June 7 this year as the date when the country's top athletes will battle for glory, and a place on Team Zimbabwe.

a1077.speaker: Tendai Tagara, NAAZ president
a1077.name: Tendai Tagara
a1077.title: NAAZ president
a1077.speech: "This is more than a national meet. It is a launchpad to continental glory. Athletes must understand that there will be no automatic selections or late trials, White City is the stage where national dreams are made."

a1077.speaker: Tendai Tagara, NAAZ president
a1077.name: Tendai Tagara
a1077.title: NAAZ president
a1077.speech: Emphasized that the selection process will be rigorous and uncompromising, saying "only those who compete at the Interprovincial Championships will be considered. There will be no shortcuts, no exceptions. This event is where we separate potential from performance." ; "The process is not just about fairness, it's about professionalism. If we are serious about building elite athletes, we must first demand elite discipline."

a1077.speaker: National Athletics Association of Zimbabwe (NAAZ)
a1077.name: National Athletics Association of Zimbabwe (NAAZ)
a1077.speech: Has issued a nationwide advisory urging all interested athletes to contact their provincial athletics representatives, while only those registered through official provincial channels will be eligible for participation.

a1101.speaker: Health Sector Reform Coalition (HSRC), Nigeria
a1101.name: Health Sector Reform Coalition (HSRC)
a1101.title: Nigeria
a1101.speech: Has urged the U.S. government to continue its leading role in tackling healthcare challenges in Africa through successful initiatives, such as the US President's Emergency Plan for AIDS Relief (PEPFAR) and support for the Global Alliance for Vaccines and Immunisation (GAVI).

a1101.speaker: Chika Offor, Coordinator of the Health Sector Reform Coalition (HSRC)
a1101.name: Chika Offor
a1101.title: Coordinator of the Health Sector Reform Coalition (HSRC)
a1101.speech: "The transformative power of initiatives like PEPFAR and GAVI is evident in the progress made in improving healthcare across Africa. The support of the U.S. in strengthening health systems has been a driving force in the fight against diseases like HIV/AIDS and malaria. While celebrating these achievements, we also want to emphasise the need for continued funding for PEPFAR and increased backing for GAVI. Their sustained financial support will strengthen the progress made so far and play a key role in further advancing healthcare outcomes throughout the continent. We urge the U.S. government to collaborate with African governments and other stakeholders to sustain these initiatives that are directly impacting millions of African lives."

a1265.speaker: White South African protesters outside the U.S. Embassy in Pretoria
a1265.name: White South African protesters outside the U.S. Embassy in Pretoria
a1265.speech: The protesters, numbering in the hundreds, carried signs that read "Thank God for President Trump" and voiced their concerns over what they see as racist policies by the South African government, which they claim discriminate against the white minority.

a1265.speaker: Willem Petzer, organizer of the protest
a1265.name: Willem Petzer
a1265.title: organizer of the protest
a1265.speech: Addressed the crowd, saying, "We just want to say to America and to the West, despite the foreign policy decisions the South African government has made over the past two decades, the West still has a friend here in South Africa."

a1265.speaker: Heinrich Steinhausen, resident and protester
a1265.name: Heinrich Steinhausen
a1265.title: resident and protester
a1265.speech: Spoke about the current state of the country, stating, "Unfortunately, the truth of the last 30 years is that we have a divided country, where government policies have positioned South Africa as a fractured nation, corrupting the concept of peace and reconciliation."

a1265.speaker: South African government
a1265.name: South African government
a1265.speech: Has rejected claims that its new laws are racially motivated, accusing Trump of spreading misinformation and distortion about the country's legal changes.

a1292.speaker: United Nations (UN)
a1292.name: United Nations (UN)
a1292.speech: has disclosed that it assisted Zambia with US$20 million last year following the declaration of the drought as a national disaster by President Hakainde Hichilema.

a1292.speaker: Beatrice Mutali, UN Resident Coordinator in Zambia
a1292.name: Beatrice Mutali
a1292.title: UN Resident Coordinator in Zambia
a1292.speech: said her organisation, the United States Agency for International Development Bureau for Humanitarian Assistance (USAID BHA) donated US$20 million to the government through the World Food Programme, targeting to support 600,000 beneficiaries in drought-affected regions.

a1302.speaker: Augustine Ngafuan, Liberia's Finance and Development Planning Minister
a1302.name: Augustine Ngafuan
a1302.title: Liberia's Finance and Development Planning Minister
a1302.speech: Has stressed the urgent need to diversify the economy to grow the country: “Diversification of our economy remains paramount because it will target low-hanging fruits in the tourism sector, which has a huge potential of driving private investment.” ; Believes that the tourism sector and agriculture sectors are highly private-sector-driven, and noted that he expects the private sector to seize the opportunity ; “Diversification of our economy is targeting low-hanging fruits in the tourism sector, which has a huge potential of driving private investment.”

a1302.speaker: Augustine Ngafuan, Liberia's Finance and Development Planning Minister
a1302.name: Augustine Ngafuan
a1302.title: Liberia's Finance and Development Planning Minister
a1302.speech: “Let me take this opportunity to welcome you all and thank you for attending this validation meeting.” ; Said the exercise is one of the last milestones in the government's roadmap to launching and implementing the new National Development Plan, dubbed the ARREST Agenda for Inclusive Development (AAID) ; Stated that the process leading to the formulation of this draft Plan has been highly consultative and inclusive from the outset: “The draft AAID we are validating today is the outcome of a series of consultative meetings we have held across the country.” ; Disclosed that the Ministry of Finance and Development Planning is grateful for the response, support, and goodwill received in the formulation process.

a1302.speaker: Augustine Ngafuan, Liberia's Finance and Development Planning Minister
a1302.name: Augustine Ngafuan
a1302.title: Liberia's Finance and Development Planning Minister
a1302.speech: Explained that the government's medium-term development agenda is largely driven by ‘ARREST’ — Agriculture with a focus on agribusiness value chains; says the medium-term agenda emphasizes roads and other infrastructure in ICT, Energy, Sea Ports, and Air Transport; that it further emphasizes good governance, especially upholding the rule of law and strengthening the fight against corruption; that it tackles the education value chain from early childhood education to basic, secondary, higher learning, and TVET; and that it targets improved health outcomes through WASH.

a1302.speaker: Augustine Ngafuan, Liberia's Finance and Development Planning Minister
a1302.name: Augustine Ngafuan
a1302.title: Liberia's Finance and Development Planning Minister
a1302.speech: Said it is important that every stakeholder has a role to play in national development.

a1302.speaker: Assistant Finance Minister for Development Planning of Liberia
a1302.name: Assistant Finance Minister for Development Planning of Liberia
a1302.speech: In a PowerPoint presentation to stakeholders, said the proposed amount announced by Minister Ngafuan for the draft development plan is a preliminary figure.

a1302.speaker: Alaric Tokpah, Acting Chairperson of the Governance Commission (Professor)
a1302.name: Alaric Tokpah
a1302.title: Acting Chairperson of the Governance Commission (Professor)
a1302.speech: In remarks, thanked the MFDP for organizing the draft ARREST agenda validation exercise and termed it a milestone in the country's development agenda: “There's no country that witnesses immense growth without proper planning, and we are grateful to form part of this exercise, which is aimed at gathering ideas for the country's national plan.”

a1534.speaker: Claude d'Almeida, conference speaker on the state of the Beninese economy
a1534.name: Claude d'Almeida
a1534.title: conference speaker on the state of the Beninese economy
a1534.speech: Said that since Benin's independence in 1960 its economy has gone through several political and economic ups and downs: during the Marxist period many positive things were done economically, but with the advent of the socialist period the country experienced many economic difficulties, translating into the government's inability to pay salaries, which created many ills within the population; the period ended with the arrival of the Bretton Woods institutions and the signing of the Structural Adjustment Programme from 1985 to 1989 ; according to the speaker, during the 1990s period of renewal characterised by the return of freedom, Benin's growth rate was fairly high and no longer negative, but the only problem is that the country was unable to move away from the directed (command) economy policy that had characterised the Marxist-Leninist period.

a1596.speaker: Dr Gloria Shirima, Senior Family Planning Advisor through the USAID Maternal and Child Health (MCH) projects
a1596.name: Dr Gloria Shirima
a1596.title: Senior Family Planning Advisor through the USAID Maternal and Child Health (MCH) projects
a1596.speech: said they will use Family Planning Week to talk to young people so that they understand the vasectomy method ; "We want them to know that what is tied are the tubes that carry male sperm to go and meet the woman's egg, to create a child, but male potency is not affected" ; said that associating misconceptions with family planning methods in various communities in the country is a reason many are blocked from using them ; "We are planning to increase the provision of education on the correct use of family planning methods, so that people understand and get rid of those misconceptions" ; said many have lacked awareness of the methods, explaining that their goal is for mothers and fathers to know which modern family planning methods they can use and for how long, and to know the minor side effects ; "We want to increase awareness because that is more of a challenge; there are those who believe that if you use family planning you get cancer, some say they will become infertile and will not be able to have children again" ; explained the benefits of family planning, that it helps the mother protect her health and that of her newborn child and helps the family plan the number of children to have over a certain period ; "Technically, at least child to child should be spaced 24 months apart at birth, and that situation gives parents the opportunity to serve their children on time and to fund school plans."

a1596.speaker: Latifa Masasi, maternal and child health services nurse at Alafa Tandika health centre
a1596.name: Latifa Masasi
a1596.title: maternal and child health services nurse at Alafa Tandika health centre
a1596.speech: said that since they began providing that education, 260 people have benefited ; "Of those, two fathers have had sterilisation, one mother, and we have continued with IUDs and injections, and those who received services were 120" ; said the enthusiasm is great, especially among food-vendor mothers, depending on the area where they provide the service, together with the many bajaji (three-wheeler) drivers ; "The fathers were more than the mothers and they got education and they had many questions; we explained to them and they understood that it is possible."

a1596.speaker: Athuman Omary, Secretary of Baba Bora (Good Fathers), Dar es Salaam Region
a1596.name: Athuman Omary
a1596.title: Secretary of Baba Bora (Good Fathers), Dar es Salaam Region
a1596.speech: urged fathers to take up that method ; "It is important for fathers too to undergo sterilisation when they feel they have reached the limit according to their life situation. Many of us used to believe that it is only mothers who should be sterilised and we fathers just use condoms" ; said that after receiving the training from the experts, men even if they undergo sterilisation are not prevented from later wanting to have children again, because they undergo a minor operation to block the sperm passages ; "After some time, if you see that you want to have children you go to have it reversed. And your manhood continues as usual and you will be performing the act as usual" ; said this is something new he has learned and he will go and be an ambassador by spreading the education in their Baba Bora groups ; "The worry was that if we undergo the operation the 'drum' will no longer work, and if that business does not work you cannot count yourself as a complete man."

a1660.speaker: Peter Ogwang, Uganda's State Minister of Sports
a1660.name: Peter Ogwang
a1660.title: Uganda's State Minister of Sports
a1660.speech: Declared that the national football team, the Cranes, deserves a victory against Bright Stars, noting the sacrifices made by Ugandans during the liberation of South Sudan ; "I know you don't know that country [South Sudan] is what it is because of our blood." ; "Some of you know very well if it was not for our brothers and sisters who died to liberate that country [South Sudan], that country [South Sudan] would not be where it is."

a1660.speaker: Peter Ogwang, Uganda's State Minister of Sports (social media post, October 14)
a1660.name: Peter Ogwang
a1660.title: Uganda's State Minister of Sports (social media post, October 14)
a1660.speech: On his social media page on October 14, referred to South Sudanese as brothers and sisters, highlighting the sacrifices of Ugandans who lost their lives during South Sudan's liberation struggle. He noted that five players on the Bright Stars National Team are "their children" who chose to represent South Sudan.

a1660.speaker: Peter Ogwang, Uganda's State Minister of Sports
a1660.name: Peter Ogwang
a1660.title: Uganda's State Minister of Sports
a1660.speech: "You know very well most of the people you are playing with are our own children from Uganda. I know about five, but they opted to play for South Sudan."

a1660.speaker: Peter Ogwang, Uganda's State Minister of Sports
a1660.name: Peter Ogwang
a1660.title: Uganda's State Minister of Sports
a1660.speech: "Our message as a government is, that we will continue to fund the national team, that is our perspective." ; "You are the only federation with special funds, make the work of Eng. Moses Mugogi easier to produce results like what you have today." ; "Please let us believe in our self and you prove it today, we need a win in Juba."

a2092.speaker: Stela Pinto Zeca, Secretary of State for Sofala province, Mozambique (press conference)
a2092.name: Stela Pinto Zeca
a2092.title: Secretary of State for Sofala province, Mozambique (press conference)
a2092.speech: Told a press conference that the bodies of a teenager and a woman were found floating in the Buzi river following flooding in the region; said the 16-year-old girl lived in the district of Buzi, in the central province of Sofala, but the woman's origin and age are not known.

a2092.speaker: Stela Pinto Zeca, Secretary of State for Sofala province, Mozambique
a2092.name: Stela Pinto Zeca
a2092.title: Secretary of State for Sofala province, Mozambique
a2092.speech: Says the floods that have hit the province since Wednesday (12.02) have already caused the removal of 70,070 people - 15,755 families - to accommodation centres or family homes located in safe areas; "We want to salute the solidarity of the many individuals who are hosting family members and others. Less than 50% of those affected are staying in accommodation centres"; added that thirty camps were created to accommodate the victims of the floods.

a2092.speaker: Stela Pinto Zeca, Secretary of State for Sofala province, Mozambique
a2092.name: Stela Pinto Zeca
a2092.title: Secretary of State for Sofala province, Mozambique
a2092.speech: "We expected to provide assistance to approximately 150,000 people, and in this case we have only 71,000 people affected, which is still within our contingency plan"; said there was capacity to provide humanitarian assistance to all victims of floods.

a2092.speaker: Local authorities in Sofala province
a2092.name: Local authorities in Sofala province
a2092.speech: Consider the affected area to be as large as 8,000 hectares.

a2092.speaker: National Institute for Disaster Management (INGC) of Mozambique
a2092.name: National Institute for Disaster Management (INGC) of Mozambique
a2092.speech: According to the INGC, the current rainy season in Mozambique, from October to April, has already killed 54 people and affected around 65,000, many of whose homes were flooded.

a2343.speaker: Blaise Ayivi, professor, representative of the Faculty of Health Sciences (FSS) of the University of Abomey-Calavi
a2343.name: Blaise Ayivi
a2343.title: professor, representative of the Faculty of Health Sciences (FSS) of the University of Abomey-Calavi
a2343.speech: According to Professor Blaise Ayivi, the programme provides for three main areas of intervention, the first concerning the strengthening of the technical capacity of targeted hospitals through the supply of appropriate medical equipment, the strengthening of the referral and counter-referral system from the community to higher-level health facilities, and capacity building through continuing training and clinical supervision of medical and paramedical staff ; said that thanks to the public-private partnership with the Vietnamese medical equipment manufacturer MTTS, the programme will provide the targeted hospitals with a complete package of technologies for the care of newborns in distress, including respiratory assistance machines, conventional and intensive phototherapy devices, warming tables, resuscitation tables, ventilation bags and masks and antibacterial gel ; states that hospitals equipped with this basic technical package will be able to treat more effectively all newborns, including premature and low-birth-weight babies and those affected by the most common conditions such as jaundice, hypothermia, respiratory distress, infections and complications of prematurity.

a2343.speaker: Kevin Armstrong, director of the USAID/Benin mission
a2343.name: Kevin Armstrong
a2343.title: director of the USAID/Benin mission
a2343.speech: After recalling the remarkable progress made in improving child survival throughout the world thanks to vaccination, family planning, nutrition and the treatment of childhood illnesses, stressed that newborn survival remains a challenge, since neonatal deaths represent a growing proportion of under-five mortality ; confirmed that the "Souffle de vie" programme will make it possible to meet the multiple challenges hospitals face in reducing neonatal mortality and morbidity, and that USAID supports the implementation of the government's policy to improve maternal and child health through a "package of high-impact interventions" ; recalled the programme's main objectives, namely to increase the availability of qualified staff to provide quality neonatal care in clinics and hospitals, to improve the availability of equipment at all levels, and to improve referral systems for newborns.

a2541.speaker: Lesetja Kganyago, SARB Governor
a2541.name: Lesetja Kganyago
a2541.title: SARB Governor
a2541.speech: Said the committee wanted to observe the full effects of previous rate reductions on the economy before making further adjustments. "The transmission of past monetary policy actions is ongoing, and we need to ensure that these measures effectively support growth while keeping inflation expectations anchored," he said.

a2541.speaker: Recent (consumer inflation) data
a2541.name: Recent (consumer inflation) data
a2541.speech: Recent data shows that consumer inflation unexpectedly cooled to 3.3% in August, down from 3.5% in July.

a2668.speaker: Senator Abubakar Kyari, Minister of Agriculture and Food Security (represented by Dr. Deola-Tayo Lordbanjou, Director, Federal Department of Agricultural Extension Services)
a2668.name: Senator Abubakar Kyari
a2668.title: Minister of Agriculture and Food Security (represented by Dr. Deola-Tayo Lordbanjou, Director, Federal Department of Agricultural Extension Services)
a2668.speech: Has stated that without efficient, impactful and responsive pluralistic agriculture extension services, Nigeria cannot transform her agricultural sector and achieve food security.

a2668.speaker: Senator Abubakar Kyari, Minister of Agriculture and Food Security
a2668.name: Senator Abubakar Kyari
a2668.title: Minister of Agriculture and Food Security
a2668.speech: Explained that the Agriculture Extension Service is a strategic vehicle for delivering innovative, effective and innovative solutions to the doorsteps of Nigerian smallholder farmers ; explained that his Ministry in the last four years has collaborated with the USAID Feed the Future Nigeria Agricultural Extension Activity to improve extension and advisory services for increased food productivity and income generation for over two million smallholder farmers in Nigeria.

a2668.speaker: Senator Abubakar Kyari, Minister of Agriculture and Food Security
a2668.name: Senator Abubakar Kyari
a2668.title: Minister of Agriculture and Food Security
a2668.speech: While commending the USAID Extension Activity for enhancing the capacity of the Micro, Small and Medium Enterprises (MSMEs) to provide most impactful agricultural practices to smallholder farmers, pointed out that since 2020 both parties have collaborated and promoted the MSME-led extension services delivery: "The parties have jointly identified several most impactful agricultural practices as business solutions for the farmers, trained MSMEs and through coaching, transformed them into extension delivery firms." ; "The parties also jointly promoted market aligned business solutions through the Agricultural Development Programmes and the States' Ministries of Agriculture, to resolve systematic challenges in extension services for smallholder farmers." ; "This partnership, therefore, not only identified business solutions for the smallholder farmers, but also integrated innovative private extension delivery approaches in the National Agricultural Extension Policy and Agricultural Extension Teaching Manual." ; "The impact of this collaboration spans new business solutions, enhanced business growth, and created jobs for both youth and women while boosting access to market for MSMEs and farmers."

a2710.speaker: UN
a2710.name: UN
a2710.speech: According to the UN, 60 percent of the country's 50 million people need humanitarian assistance.

a2710.speaker: Doctors Without Borders (MSF)
a2710.name: Doctors Without Borders (MSF)
a2710.speech: reiterates its calls on the warring parties and their allies to ensure that civilians, humanitarian personnel, and medical teams are protected and that all restrictions are removed on the movements of humanitarian supplies and staff, especially as the rainy season fast approaches.

a2710.speaker: Claire San Filippo, MSF Emergency Coordinator
a2710.name: Claire San Filippo
a2710.title: MSF Emergency Coordinator
a2710.speech: "The warring parties are not only failing to protect civilians - they are actively compounding their suffering." ; "Wherever you look in Sudan, you will find needs - overwhelming, urgent, and unmet. Millions are receiving almost no humanitarian assistance, medical facilities and staff remain under attack, and the global humanitarian system is failing to deliver even a fraction of what's required."

a2710.speaker: UN
a2710.name: UN
a2710.speech: Widespread starvation is taking hold, according to the UN - Sudan is currently the only place in the world where famine has been officially declared in multiple locations.

a2710.speaker: Marta Cazorla, MSF Emergency Coordinator
a2710.name: Marta Cazorla
a2710.title: MSF Emergency Coordinator
a2710.speech: "Outbreaks of measles, cholera and diphtheria are spreading, driven by poor living conditions and disrupted vaccination campaigns. Mental health support and care for survivors of sexual violence remain painfully limited. These compounding crises reflect not just the brutality of the conflict, but the dire consequences of the crumbling public healthcare system and a failing humanitarian response."

a2710.speaker: UN
a2710.name: UN
a2710.speech: More than 13 million people have been displaced by the conflict, according to the UN - many of them multiple times; 8.9 million remain displaced inside Sudan, while 3.9 million have crossed into neighbouring countries.

a2710.speaker: World Health Organization (WHO)
a2710.name: World Health Organization (WHO)
a2710.speech: According to the WHO, more than 70 percent of health facilities in conflict-affected areas are barely operational or completely closed, leaving millions without access to critical care.

a2710.speaker: MSF (records/data)
a2710.name: MSF (records/data)
a2710.speech: Since the war began, MSF has recorded over 80 violent incidents targeting our staff, infrastructure, vehicles and supplies.

a2710.speaker: Muhammad Yusuf Ishaq Abdullah, MSF health promotion officer in Tawila, North Darfur
a2710.name: Muhammad Yusuf Ishaq Abdullah
a2710.title: MSF health promotion officer in Tawila, North Darfur
a2710.speech: "Buildings were destroyed, even beds were looted, and medicines were burned to the ground. From afar, it looked like a hospital, but when you entered it, it was a shelter for snakes and grass," said about the state of Tawila's hospital after being attacked and looted in June 2023.

a2710.speaker: Doctors Without Borders (MSF)
a2710.name: Doctors Without Borders (MSF)
a2710.speech: calls for immediate preparedness measures ahead of the rainy season: more border crossings must be opened, and key roads and bridges must be repaired and kept accessible, especially in Darfur. MSF urges all actors - including donors, governments, and UN agencies - to enable and prioritize the aid delivery, ensuring that assistance not only reaches the country but is transported swiftly and safely to the hardest-hit and most remote communities.

a2908.speaker: Mohamed Mchengerwa, Minister of State, President’s Office – Regional Administration and Local Government
a2908.name: Mohamed Mchengerwa
a2908.title: Minister of State, President’s Office – Regional Administration and Local Government
a2908.speech: Has said that the government has allocated 18bn/- for purchase of ICT equipment in the 2023/2024 financial year, allocated by recognising the importance of using ICT in learning and building the intended competencies in secondary school curricula, and said the aim of providing the equipment was to strengthen modern teaching and learning methods by utilising and learning ICT, in order to keep up with global advancements in science and technology ; “Through the implementation of the SEQUIP project, a total of 1,500 secondary schools are expected to benefit from ICT equipment. Today, we are distributing equipment to 231 schools, which are part of the 1,500 schools that will benefit from this programme” ; said the use of ICT equipment is one of the interventions and indicators of the implementation of the SEQUIP programme ; said the training for the teachers aims to ensure they are equipped with the skills to maintain the purchased equipment, use it effectively, guide students and perform basic troubleshooting when equipment malfunctions, and added that the purchase of ICT equipment has followed the SEQUIP (ICT package) guidelines ; “The government believes that the use of ICT equipment, which is being distributed today, will bring about a major transformation in teaching and learning in secondary schools” ; noted that with the tools provided, teachers will enhance their teaching effectiveness and students will gain additional knowledge during their learning process.

a2912.speaker: Grey Frandsen, Kelly Matzen and Neil Morrison (Oxitec), and Dr Bouh Abdi and Dr Abdoul-Ilah Ahmed, project initiators (coordinator and health adviser to the Head of State, and programme supervisor)
a2912.name: Grey Frandsen
a2912.title: Kelly Matzen and Neil Morrison (Oxitec), and Dr Bouh Abdi and Dr Abdoul-Ilah Ahmed, project initiators (coordinator and health adviser to the Head of State, and programme supervisor)
a2912.speech: Led the presentations at the round table, reporting that various stages of the programme have been completed and validated, such as the monitoring and knowledge of the Anopheles stephensi vector in Djibouti, that data on its behaviour and ecology have been acquired and will be useful in the deployment phases, that the strains of Djibouti's allied mosquitoes have been developed and are being reared in an insectary with a preliminary pilot deployment stage being prepared, and that the awareness-raising and “community engagement” stages at the study and planned deployment sites are robust and under way; referring to the use of the technology in Brazil for Aedes aegypti, where a 94% suppression of the vector was recorded, they said the development of this technology for Anopheles stephensi in Djibouti bodes well for the fight against malaria.

a2912.speaker: Ministry of Health of Djibouti (source of the report)
a2912.name: Ministry of Health of Djibouti (source of the report)
a2912.speech: Cited as the source of the article reporting the round table on the “mosquito ally of Djibouti” programme.

a3107.speaker: Ambassador Carlos Duarte, Brazil’s Secretary for Africa and the Middle East in the Ministry of Foreign Affairs
a3107.name: Ambassador Carlos Duarte
a3107.title: Brazil’s Secretary for Africa and the Middle East in the Ministry of Foreign Affairs
a3107.speech: Announced a donation of over N$2 million by Brazil through the World Food Program, funds which will help Namibia improve food security, create employment, and strengthen socio-economic development ; highlighted potential areas of cooperation.

a3107.speaker: Penda Naanda, Executive Director in Namibia’s Ministry of International Relations and Cooperation
a3107.name: Penda Naanda
a3107.title: Executive Director in Namibia’s Ministry of International Relations and Cooperation
a3107.speech: Expressed gratitude for Brazil’s continuous humanitarian assistance.

a3107.speaker: Penda Naanda, Executive Director in Namibia’s Ministry of International Relations and Cooperation
a3107.name: Penda Naanda
a3107.title: Executive Director in Namibia’s Ministry of International Relations and Cooperation
a3107.speech: Congratulated Brazil for the G20 Presidency position, stating that it makes a difference for Africa, which historically has been left out ; welcomed Brazil’s sentiments on the reform of international institutions such as the UN Security Council.

a3107.speaker: Penda Naanda, Executive Director in Namibia’s Ministry of International Relations and Cooperation
a3107.name: Penda Naanda
a3107.title: Executive Director in Namibia’s Ministry of International Relations and Cooperation
a3107.speech: Advocates for more women to be involved in military and police cooperation with Brazil.

a3136.speaker: Research published in ‘The Lancet’ medical journal
a3136.name: Research published in ‘The Lancet’ medical journal
a3136.speech: has indicated that Donald Trump’s decision to cut aid for the US funding towards foreign humanitarian efforts could lead to more than 14 million additional deaths by 2030; according to the findings, children are at a greater risk of premature death, and that includes over 4.5 million children under the age of five, or around 700,000 child deaths a year; statistics show that data from 133 nations estimated that USAID funding had prevented 91 million deaths in developing countries between 2001 and 2021.

a3136.speaker: UN official (anonymous)
a3136.name: UN official (anonymous)
a3136.speech: Last month, a UN official told the BBC that hundreds of thousands of people were “slowly starving” in Kenyan refugee camps after US funding cuts reduced food rations to their lowest ever levels.

a3210.speaker: Elon Musk, head of the Department of Government Efficiency (DOGE)
a3210.name: Elon Musk
a3210.title: head of the Department of Government Efficiency (DOGE)
a3210.speech: Announcing his organization’s action on his X platform on Monday: “Among many other things, @DOGE today canceled a $17M project to provide tax policy advice to Liberia.” ; “Why would anyone think that this is a good use of YOUR tax money?”

a3210.speaker: Key Yarkpazuo Sr. (Liberian commenter)
a3210.name: Key Yarkpazuo Sr. (Liberian commenter)
a3210.speech: “17 million dollars could have helped the Health Sector. I think we requested the wrong help from USAID. While it’s true we need help with improving our tax generating system(s), there are sectors that should be priority when reaching out for help. Not sure they would’ve completely canceled help for education, health, agriculture or farm to market roads.”

a3210.speaker: Vikpalah Alfred Tartee (Liberian commenter)
a3210.name: Vikpalah Alfred Tartee (Liberian commenter)
a3210.speech: “Elon Musk is beating senses into the heads of aid-dependent nations, like Liberia and others. He’s on a mission to protect the US resources and put the American interests first. That’s his priority. However, our government needs to act fast – cut down salaries and benefits across all sectors. President Boakai shouldn’t have the mindset that President Trump and Elon would listen to diplomatic talks. They are more radical than diplomatic. These Republicans are on a mission to Make America Great Again.”

a3210.speaker: Sneh T. Weah (Liberian commenter)
a3210.name: Sneh T. Weah (Liberian commenter)
a3210.speech: “The United States provides 17m in tax policy advice, over 12m goes back to the US economy through salaries and benefits of American tax experts employed with the project. What’s big here? When Dr. Robtel Neajai Pailey talked about ‘re-imagining Liberia’, you guys were making mockery.”

a3210.speaker: Jonah De Real Dolo (Liberian commenter)
a3210.name: Jonah De Real Dolo (Liberian commenter)
a3210.speech: “Simple logic. Instead, they will continue to have DSA, fat allowances plus many other useless financial misappropriations and still feel that begging is the gateway to the growth and development of the Liberian economy. Law makers are at the full front of wasteful spending in our economy and it’s about time they think twice and do the needful. Some of them only have the audacity to criticize on radio or facebook but quickly go to the executive to beg for slots and provide names for recommendations. Once the government refuses to take their multiple names provided for appointment in government then they start to criticize the government in a baseless manner. Cc… Sen. Amara Konneh of the Liberian senate.”

a3210.speaker: Patrick N. Dagbe (Liberian commenter)
a3210.name: Patrick N. Dagbe (Liberian commenter)
a3210.speech: “Elon is making a lot of sense here. While it’s true that we need to urgently cut down waste so as to adequately adjust to pressing ongoing international diplomatic and political developments, I also think that those kinds of budget allotments from USAID’S budget lines which says, USAID provides the knowledge and again USAID pay for the knowledge being provided, speaks to something suspicious within the budget formation of USAID at the executive level.”

a3210.speaker: Boakai Jaleiba (Liberian commenter)
a3210.name: Boakai Jaleiba (Liberian commenter)
a3210.speech: “Martin, some of your colleagues who recently left MFDP and LRA are employed with that program, and they are all going to lose their jobs. This is bad news.”

a3210.speaker: Martin K.N. Kollie (Liberian commenter/activist)
a3210.name: Martin K.N. Kollie (Liberian commenter/activist)
a3210.speech: “Very bad news. This is why President Boakai should be decisive and bold right now about cutting down on public wastage. We can’t be aid dependent forever while a few greedy and corrupt politicians bag tens of millions every year in fat salaries and benefits amid extreme hardship and over 90% unemployment. Let them cap all salaries and benefits at $5K.”

a3210.speaker: Donald Trump, US President
a3210.name: Donald Trump
a3210.title: US President
a3210.speech: In August 2024, Trump said at a campaign event that, if he were elected, he would be open to giving Musk an advisory role.

a3210.speaker: Elon Musk (post on X)
a3210.name: Elon Musk (post on X)
a3210.speech: Wrote a post on X saying, “I am willing to serve”, along with an AI-created image of him standing in front of a lectern marked “Department of Government Efficiency”.

a3210.speaker: Executive order establishing DOGE (US government document)
a3210.name: Executive order establishing DOGE (US government document)
a3210.speech: According to the executive order that established it, its formal purpose is to “modernize federal technology and software to maximize governmental efficiency and productivity”.

a3215.speaker: Ulaç Demirag, IFAD Country Director for Ethiopia
a3215.name: Ulaç Demirag
a3215.title: IFAD Country Director for Ethiopia
a3215.speech: “Access to finance is crucial for rural people – particularly those whose incomes are threatened by a changing climate – to expand their businesses, and to take advantage of new emerging livelihood opportunities along agricultural and agro-industrial value chain” ; “This new programme will provide financial products and services to poor rural people in the least developed areas to promote poverty reduction and livelihood risk mitigation.”

a3234.speaker: Africa Intelligence (think tank)
a3234.name: Africa Intelligence (think tank)
a3234.speech: According to think tank Africa Intelligence, the strategy is to pull from a wider pool of global and local investors.

a3234.speaker: Joao Lourenco, President of Angola
a3234.name: Joao Lourenco
a3234.title: President of Angola
a3234.speech: Announced the summit at a recent BRICS meeting, highlighting the strategic diversification.

a3383.speaker: NGO Regulatory Authority (Ngora) survey, ‘Assessment report on the effects of the USAid and donor funding freeze on the NGO sector in Malawi’
a3383.name: NGO Regulatory Authority (Ngora) survey
a3383.title: ‘Assessment report on the effects of the USAid and donor funding freeze on the NGO sector in Malawi’
a3383.speech: Has established that non-governmental organisations in the health sector are the worst affected by the USAid aid cut, with 77.14 percent of the surveyed organisations reporting disruptions in implementation of health projects and all 28 districts reporting ongoing or planned project activities affected by the aid withdrawal: “Districts such as Lilongwe, Blantyre, Mangochi, Zomba and Mzimba are among the most impacted, given their concentration of USAid-supported health interventions, including HIV and Aids, maternal and child health and disease prevention programmes.”

a3383.speaker: NGO Regulatory Authority (Ngora) assessment report
a3383.name: NGO Regulatory Authority (Ngora) assessment report
a3383.speech: Says the survey targeted 250 NGOs registered under the NGO Act, of which 151 responded (a 60 percent response rate) which Ngora says provided a reasonably strong foundation for drawing insights, and that of the 151 there were 38, representing 25.2 percent, which reported direct negative impacts ; establishes that the second most affected sector is gender, youth and development as reported by 40 percent of the NGOs, with education, research and development third at 22.86 percent.

a3383.speaker: NGO Regulatory Authority (Ngora) assessment report
a3383.name: NGO Regulatory Authority (Ngora) assessment report
a3383.speech: “A notable 58.3 percent of NGOs reported the closure of specific programmes, with the health and education sectors being particularly affected. Fifty-two percent experienced delays in the implementation of planned activities, while 47.2 percent were forced to scale down the scope or reach of their initiatives due to budget constraints. Human resource capacities were also affected, as 50 percent of the organisations reduced their workforce. Of these, 63.6 percent implemented modest staff reductions of between 0 to 20 percent, while 18.2 percent undertook more drastic measures, cutting over 60 percent of their personnel.” ; observes that 85.7 percent of the surveyed NGOs reported that their beneficiaries experienced negative consequences, including reduced access to life-saving health services, termination of school support and nutrition programmes, and significant disruption to humanitarian relief efforts in disaster-prone regions.

a3383.speaker: Edward Chileka Banda, Ngora chief executive officer
a3383.name: Edward Chileka Banda
a3383.title: Ngora chief executive officer
a3383.speech: Speaking in an interview, advised NGOs to engage in economic activities such as production in order to navigate through the funding cuts from various development partners: “We have NGOs, for example, those involved in school feeding programmes. They just need maize flour to provide porridge for learners. They have been depending on donors to buy maize. It is possible for such NGOs to produce maize. Maybe they can just engage their donor to assist with farm inputs.”

a3383.speaker: George Jobe, Malawi Health Equity Network executive director
a3383.name: George Jobe
a3383.title: Malawi Health Equity Network executive director
a3383.speech: Expressed worry that many health personnel are now jobless following the US aid freeze.

a3383.speaker: National Planning Commission (NPC) and International Food Policy Research Institute (Ifpri) study, released May 2025
a3383.name: National Planning Commission (NPC) and International Food Policy Research Institute (Ifpri) study
a3383.title: released May 2025
a3383.speech: Showed that as of March 2025, at least 4 451 healthcare staff relying on US-funding had their contracts terminated.

a3398.speaker: Michael Ryan, WHO Deputy Director-General
a3398.name: Michael Ryan
a3398.title: WHO Deputy Director-General
a3398.speech: Is indignant: "I remind you all that the United States government is not leaving a building in Geneva. It is not leaving a secretariat in Geneva. It is leaving a community of nations. It is essentially... it is essentially a break with you, not with me. And that must be taken into account by the 193 member states represented here today."

a3398.speaker: Tedros Adhanom Ghebreyesus, WHO Director-General
a3398.name: Tedros Adhanom Ghebreyesus
a3398.title: WHO Director-General
a3398.speech: "Nevertheless, it will be very important to invest in the return of the United States. And on this point, I think each one of you can play, can play, a role."

a3398.speaker: An analyst (unnamed)
a3398.name: An analyst (unnamed)
a3398.speech: Worries that interventions in the Middle East, in Ukraine and in Sudan are threatened, not to mention hundreds of millions of dollars lost by the polio eradication and HIV programmes since the announcement of the freeze on American development aid worldwide.

a3530.speaker: European Training Foundation
a3530.name: European Training Foundation
a3530.speech: According to the European Training Foundation, the US Government was the largest single donor of aid in the world in 2023, disbursing over US$80 billion across 208 countries; the US$64 billion in economic assistance accounted for approximately 30 per cent of global Official Development Assistance (ODA), and the US was also responsible for more than 40 per cent of the world’s humanitarian aid, impacting everything from disaster relief to health services.

a3530.speaker: Dr Tedros Adhanom Ghebreyesus, World Health Organisation Director-General
a3530.name: Dr Tedros Adhanom Ghebreyesus
a3530.title: World Health Organisation Director-General
a3530.speech: Recently warned of an escalating crisis: “people running out of food, hospitals closing and nations facing urgent medicine shortages”.

a3710.speaker: Prof. Sidikou Ramatou Djermakoye Seyni, Minister of Population, Social Action and National Solidarity of Niger
a3710.name: Prof. Sidikou Ramatou Djermakoye Seyni
a3710.title: Minister of Population, Social Action and National Solidarity of Niger
a3710.speech: In a message delivered on Monday 18 August 2025, on the eve of World Humanitarian Day, reaffirmed Niger's commitment to working for humanitarian action centred on national sovereignty, aligned with the country's priorities and focused on the real needs of communities: “Since 2010, Niger has marked this day to honour the courage and commitment of these women and men who, every day, choose to commit themselves to saving lives” ; “the 2025 edition is being held in a global context still marked by complex security crises, forced displacement of populations, as well as increasingly frequent climate shocks” ; “given the persistence, and even the worsening, of these crises, the theme ‘Act for Humanity’ has been carried over again this year”, underscoring “the urgency of continuing to protect civilian populations, to guarantee access to essential services, and to preserve humanitarian space in a world where violence increasingly targets the innocent” ; said the theme also calls for “increased mobilization of the world's decision-makers so that they use their powers to put an end to this human tragedy” ; “Niger remains determined to work for humanitarian action anchored in national sovereignty, aligned with the country's priorities and centred on the real needs of communities.”

a3710.speaker: Prof. Sidikou Ramatou Djermakoye Seyni, Minister of Population, Social Action and National Solidarity of Niger
a3710.name: Prof. Sidikou Ramatou Djermakoye Seyni
a3710.title: Minister of Population, Social Action and National Solidarity of Niger
a3710.speech: Recalled that “in regions such as the central Sahel, and notably in the countries of the Alliance of Sahel States (AES), terrorist armed groups, without faith or law, gratuitously attack civilians every day, disrupting the life of communities and compromising their access to security, education, health and livelihoods”, noting that in Niger “humanitarian challenges remain significant; despite the considerable efforts of the national authorities and partners, persistent insecurity, notably in certain border areas, continues to cause displacement – refugees and internally displaced persons – and makes access to basic services difficult for many families” ; noted that “these actions demonstrate the capacity of the State and of communities to adapt, to anticipate and to build lasting resilience. Beyond the response to the flood crisis, they take into account many other issues such as food and nutrition security” ; said the actions carried out by the Nigerien government amount to “strengthening resilience in the face of food and nutritional insecurity, and to the establishment of the National Plan of Responses to Food and Nutritional Insecurity (PNRIAN) in 2023, a reference document for the prevention of and response to food, nutritional and pastoral insecurity”.

a3710.speaker: Prof. Sidikou Ramatou Djermakoye Seyni, Minister of Population, Social Action and National Solidarity of Niger
a3710.name: Prof. Sidikou Ramatou Djermakoye Seyni
a3710.title: Minister of Population, Social Action and National Solidarity of Niger
a3710.speech: Paid “emphatic tribute to all those who commit themselves, sometimes at the peril of their lives, to come to the aid of those who suffer”: “You are the living proof that hope can be reborn, even in the most difficult contexts”, she said to humanitarian actors, before expressing the government's “deep gratitude” for their “commitment alongside the Nigerien people”, while calling on them “to pursue their efforts with rigour and humanity, in respect of the principles of transparency, accountability and above all the dignity of the people of this country”.

a3728.speaker: United States (vote at the United Nations)
a3728.name: United States (vote at the United Nations)
a3728.speech: Voted “NO” to a United Nations resolution calling for UN cooperation with the Council of Europe, while condemning “Russian aggression in Ukraine”; the United States voted in line with Russia and other friendly countries, including Belarus, Eritrea, Mali, Nicaragua, Niger, North Korea and Sudan.

a3746.speaker: Reno Omokri, social and public affairs commentator
a3746.name: Reno Omokri
a3746.title: social and public affairs commentator
