a3746.speech: Dismissed the allegations by Binance executive Tigran Gambarya against Nigeria's National Security Adviser Nuhu Ribadu, calling them a “false flag operation” designed to deflect attention from a significant disclosure regarding alleged U.S. financial support of Boko Haram through USAID ; “This is a deliberate distraction,” Omokri stated in a viral social media post ; He wrote: “The lies by Tigran Gambarya against Malam Nuhu Ribadu and the Office of the National Security Adviser are a deliberate distraction designed to deflect attention from the terror funding scandal involving USAID. Discerning Nigerians may have noticed that Mr. Gambarya made his wild allegations precisely an hour after Republican U.S. Congressman Scott Perry revealed that certain U.S. high officials had been funding Boko Haram... This is a man who has been roaming free in the United States for weeks. Why now? This is a typical distraction strategy, and Nigeria should not fall for it. The swamp is desperate and, therefore, clutching at straws. Malam Nuhu Ribadu is an incorruptible leader who, as Chairman of the Economic and Financial Crimes Commission, refused a $15 million cash bribe in 2006 and instead deposited the funds at the Central Bank of Nigeria. Tigran Gambarya is an allegedly corrupt economic saboteur who worked against Nigeria's economic interests for people who Congressman Perry has now exposed as funders of terror. Who should you believe? The answer is obvious. This is a pure case of corruption fighting back!”

a3746.speaker: Scott Perry, Republican U.S. Congressman
a3746.name: Scott Perry
a3746.title: Republican U.S. Congressman
a3746.speech: Alleged that certain American officials had been funding Boko Haram through the United States Agency for International Development (USAID).

a3746.speaker: Tigran Gambarya, Binance executive
a3746.name: Tigran Gambarya
a3746.title: Binance executive
a3746.speech: Made allegations against Nigeria's National Security Adviser, Malam Nuhu Ribadu, and the Office of the National Security Adviser, posted on X.

a3764.speaker: Perry Scott, of the United States parliament
a3764.name: Perry Scott
a3764.title: of the United States parliament
a3764.speech: Alleged the funding of terrorism in Nigeria by the United States Agency for International Development (USAID).

a3764.speaker: Mohammed Ali Ndume, Senator representing Borno South Senatorial District
a3764.name: Mohammed Ali Ndume
a3764.title: Senator representing Borno South Senatorial District
a3764.speech: Raised an Order of Urgent National Security through Order 41 and urged the Senate to consider the revelation as too weighty to gloss over, given the devastation that terrorists have done to the country, particularly the Boko Haram fighters, stressing that the investigation would put paid to speculations on how the non-state actors have been surviving over the years.

a3764.speaker: Godswill Akpabio, Senate President
a3764.name: Godswill Akpabio
a3764.title: Senate President
a3764.speech: In sustaining the resolution, remarked that security issues should not be discussed in the market, noting that the head of security intelligence will offer the Senate better perspective in a closed door meeting with them.

a3957.speaker: Sheila Mudenda, Zambia Statistics Agency (ZamStats) acting statistician-general
a3957.name: Sheila Mudenda
a3957.title: Zambia Statistics Agency (ZamStats) acting statistician-general
a3957.speech: Said export earnings from refined copper decreased by 0.3 percentage point from K19.7 billion in March to K19.6 billion in April ; "Refined copper export volumes increased by 1.6 percent, from 71,200 tonnes in March 2025 to 72,300 tonnes in April 2025. Further, copper prices on the London Metal Exchange (LME) market for the corresponding months decreased by 5.5 percent, from US$9,731.1 per tonne in March 2025 to US$9,192.1 in April 2025," said in a presentation read by the chief statistician, Chola Daka.

a4000.speaker: Microsoft (company statement)
a4000.name: Microsoft (company statement)
a4000.speech: Said Chinese “threat actors” have hacked Microsoft’s SharePoint document software servers and targeted the data of the businesses using it; said China state-backed Linen Typhoon and Violet Typhoon as well as China-based Storm-2603 “exploited vulnerabilities” in on-premises SharePoint servers, the kind used by firms, but not in its cloud-based service ; “Investigations into other actors also using these exploits are still ongoing” ; said it had “high confidence” the hackers would continue to target systems which have not installed its security updates, and that it would update its website blog with more information as its investigation continues ; said it had observed attacks in which hackers had sent a request to a SharePoint server “enabling the theft of the key material by threat actors”.

a4000.speaker: Microsoft (company statement)
a4000.name: Microsoft (company statement)
a4000.speech: Said Linen Typhoon had “focused on stealing intellectual property, primarily targeting organizations related to government, defence, strategic planning, and human rights” for 13 years; added that Violet Typhoon had been “dedicated to espionage”, primarily targeting former government and military staff, non-governmental organizations, think tanks, higher education, the media, the financial sector and the health sector in the US, Europe, and East Asia; and that Storm-2603 was “assessed with medium confidence to be a China-based threat actor”.

a4000.speaker: Charles Carmakal, chief technology officer at Mandiant Consulting (a division of Google Cloud)
a4000.name: Charles Carmakal
a4000.title: chief technology officer at Mandiant Consulting (a division of Google Cloud)
a4000.speech: Told the BBC it was “aware of several victims in several different sectors across a number of global geographies” ; said it appeared that governments and businesses that use SharePoint on their sites were the primary target, and that a number of adversaries who stole material encoded by cryptography were then able to regain ongoing access to the victims’ SharePoint data ; “This was exploited in a very broad way, very opportunistically before a patch was made available. That’s why this is significant” ; said the “China-nexus actor” was deploying techniques similar to previous campaigns associated with Beijing.

a4052.speaker: International Monetary Fund (IMF) (statement)
a4052.name: International Monetary Fund (IMF) (statement)
a4052.speech: reported in a statement yesterday that the country's economy is on solid footing, growing 5.4 per cent in the first quarter of 2025, driven by strong performance in the mining sector, alongside healthy activity in agriculture, manufacturing, construction and a recovery in tourism and services.

a4052.speaker: Nicolas Blancher, IMF mission leader
a4052.name: Nicolas Blancher
a4052.title: IMF mission leader
a4052.speech: "Economic activity remains robust, driven by strong mining sector growth and healthy activity in agriculture, manufacturing and construction, while inflation has remained low."

a4052.speaker: International Monetary Fund (IMF)
a4052.name: International Monetary Fund (IMF)
a4052.speech: noted that structural reforms are progressing but emphasised the need to accelerate them to navigate global challenges, enhance climate resilience and boost long-term growth potential ; also highlighted the Medium-Term Revenue Strategy, which will enhance revenue mobilisation and create fiscal space for investment in human capital.

a4052.speaker: International Monetary Fund (IMF) (statement)
a4052.name: International Monetary Fund (IMF) (statement)
a4052.speech: "Despite a positive outlook, risks are tilted to the downside, including a slowdown in the global economy and trade, geoeconomic fragmentation and reduced foreign development assistance." ; warned that upcoming national elections could increase fiscal pressures and slow reforms, while insufficient and erratic rainfall may affect growth and inflation.

a4052.speaker: International Monetary Fund (IMF)
a4052.name: International Monetary Fund (IMF)
a4052.speech: said that in 2025/26, strict implementation of the approved budget will be essential to create fiscal space for social spending while preserving debt sustainability.

a4052.speaker: International Monetary Fund (IMF)
a4052.name: International Monetary Fund (IMF)
a4052.speech: "Continuing to enhance exchange rate flexibility will be critical for the development of the interbank FX market."

a4052.speaker: Dr Hildebrand Shayo, economist and investment banker
a4052.name: Dr Hildebrand Shayo
a4052.title: economist and investment banker
a4052.speech: told the "Daily News" that the upcoming elections could heighten demands for fiscal easing, while climate variability and erratic rainfall pose risks to agricultural output and inflation. "The upcoming General Elections will likely intensify demands for fiscal easing or delay reforms. Climate variability and erratic rainfall could also affect agricultural output and contribute to inflationary pressures."

a4071.speaker: “What We Know About Exit – Practical Guidance For Developing Exit Strategies in the Field”, publication of the C-SAFE Regional Learning Spaces Initiative by Alison Gardner, Kara Greenblott and Erika Joubert
a4071.name: “What We Know About Exit – Practical Guidance For Developing Exit Strategies in the Field”
a4071.title: publication of the C-SAFE Regional Learning Spaces Initiative by Alison Gardner, Kara Greenblott and Erika Joubert
a4071.speech: Cited as the source for the definition that a program “exit” refers to the withdrawal of all externally provided program resources from an entire program area, and that a program Exit Strategy is a plan describing how the program intends to withdraw its resources while ensuring that achievement of the program goals (relief or development) is not jeopardized and that progress towards these goals will continue; it sets out three basic approaches to Exit Strategies — phasing down (a gradual reduction of program activities, utilizing local organizations to sustain program benefits while the original sponsor deploys fewer resources), phasing out (a sponsor's withdrawal of involvement in a program without turning it over to another institution), and phasing over (a sponsor transfers program activities to local institutions or communities, with emphasis on institutional capacity building).

a4071.speaker: “What We Know About Exit – Practical Guidance For Developing Exit Strategies in the Field”, publication of the C-SAFE Regional Learning Spaces Initiative (an initiative by CARE, World Vision, CRS, ADRA and USAID)
a4071.name: “What We Know About Exit – Practical Guidance For Developing Exit Strategies in the Field”
a4071.title: publication of the C-SAFE Regional Learning Spaces Initiative (an initiative by CARE, World Vision, CRS, ADRA and USAID)
a4071.speech: Cited as the source for the criteria used to determine when to exit programs, grouped into three general categories — time limit, achievement of program impacts, and achievement of benchmarks — and for the recommendations that establishing an exit timeline linked to the program funding cycle and clearly communicated to the community is essential, that the exit plan remain flexible, that exit plans be implemented in a gradual, phased manner, that continued contact with communities after phase over or phase out helps support sustainability of outcomes, that ongoing and timely monitoring of benchmarks is critical and should be integrated into the overall program's monitoring and evaluation plan, and that an evaluation should be conducted after a period of time has elapsed following the program exit.

a4082.speaker: Donald Trump, US President (Executive Order 14169)
a4082.name: Donald Trump
a4082.title: US President (Executive Order 14169)
a4082.speech: On 20 January 2025 issued an executive order to halt all foreign aid and disbursements, except for food assistance, affecting the Agency for International Development (USAID).

a4082.speaker: Marco Rubio, US Secretary of State
a4082.name: Marco Rubio
a4082.title: US Secretary of State
a4082.speech: In March, announced that the Trump administration had cancelled 83 per cent of USAID's programme. Mr Rubio said the agency had disbursed over $715 billion over the years, and now America is redirecting the funding into domestic affairs.

a4082.speaker: The Global Fund office in Nigeria
a4082.name: The Global Fund office in Nigeria
a4082.speech: Says the country needs $404 million to deliver TB treatment and services in 2025.

a4082.speaker: Ibrahim Tajudeen, Executive Secretary of the Global Fund Country Coordination Mechanism (CCM) in Nigeria
a4082.name: Ibrahim Tajudeen
a4082.title: Executive Secretary of the Global Fund Country Coordination Mechanism (CCM) in Nigeria
a4082.speech: In March, said the TB drugs allocated for 2025 had been used to meet the treatment demands for 2024. He disclosed that the US funding withdrawal has created a $5 million funding gap.

a4082.speaker: Nurse at the chest clinic, State Specialist Hospital, Ashubiaro, Osogbo (unnamed)
a4082.name: Nurse at the chest clinic
a4082.title: State Specialist Hospital, Ashubiaro, Osogbo (unnamed)
a4082.speech: "You're wasting our efforts, and that is not good enough" ; "We told you to stop drinking alcohol and herbal concoctions. Your tests and drugs are expensive, but you get them free. We're helping you, but you've refused to help yourself."

a4082.speaker: Osun State official in charge of TB programmes (anonymous)
a4082.name: Osun State official in charge of TB programmes (anonymous)
a4082.speech: Said donors used to pay drug-resistant patients monthly for the period of free treatment to encourage them, starting from N3,000 ($2), then N6,000 ($4), N10,000 ($7), N25,000 ($17) and later N35,000 ($23). "They were mostly poor locals, and they complained that they didn't have money for transport from their house to the clinic. They also complained that they didn't have money for food because most of their family members had abandoned them for fear of infection. We also give them food just to encourage them to comply." ; "They can't work during treatment, and they often hate themselves because of the disease. They hardly move around because of the stigma. Everyone avoids them, and they don't want to be seen in places where they are known. The money we gave them might not be enough to feed them in a month, but it really encouraged them to buy some nutritious food and come to the clinic often."

a4082.speaker: Osun State TB official (anonymous)
a4082.name: Osun State TB official (anonymous)
a4082.speech: Said all the equipment used for TB was imported and paid for by donors who got their funds from the American government, including digital x-ray machines, rapid diagnostic kits, GeneXpert machines, TruNat, and other radiological tools. "We have a shortage of reporting and recording tools. The sector was already struggling with low staff. Before, there was no counterpart funding from the government for these programmes, as we solely relied on donors. Now, the government is trying to recruit more officials." ; "The workload is much, and it is not possible to cover the areas of the partners who left, which is the reason the cases dropped, as we could not detect more. We had a shortage of drugs last quarter; we got a supply in the second quarter. Due to low case detection, there are still drugs. Our data is coming down because of the funding withdrawal. We screen patients all over; now, nobody is there to screen them. So, the case will go down to zero." ; "In Q3 of 2024, in Osun, there were over 7,000 cases. We were trying to bring it up when the US executive order came early this year, and it brought the number down. Q1 2025 was 4,525. We're currently collating the numbers for Q2 2025, and we can't tell what the present data says. It might be less." ; "TB is an airborne disease. We are sitting on a keg of gun powder which can explode anytime."

a4082.speaker: 2021 national guidelines for the management of TB/HIV co-infection in Nigeria (policy document)
a4082.name: 2021 national guidelines for the management of TB/HIV co-infection in Nigeria (policy document)
a4082.speech: HIV is known to increase the burden of TB, while TB is the leading cause of death among people living with HIV and was responsible for one-third of the estimated 690,000 deaths from HIV in 2019.

a4082.speaker: National Strategic Plan for Tuberculosis Control 2021-2025 (policy document)
a4082.name: National Strategic Plan for Tuberculosis Control 2021-2025 (policy document)
a4082.speech: Says the domestic funding for TB control in Nigeria is very low, stating that only 8 per cent of TB interventions are funded locally, while 32 per cent is funded by international donors, leaving an existing gap of 60 per cent of the required funding for TB programmes.

a4082.speaker: Bola Tinubu, President of Nigeria
a4082.name: Bola Tinubu
a4082.title: President of Nigeria
a4082.speech: In May, while addressing a joint session of the National Assembly, said no amount of foreign aid would help Nigeria unless citizens unite to build the country. "No amount of aid from foreign countries can help us. Let us work together to build our nation, charting a new path."

a4082.speaker: Alaba Balogun, Head of Press and Public Relations, Federal Ministry of Health (non-response)
a4082.name: Alaba Balogun
a4082.title: Head of Press and Public Relations, Federal Ministry of Health (non-response)
a4082.speech: TheCable contacted him asking questions on what the Nigerian government is doing to bridge the gap left behind by foreign donors and if domestic funding has actually been released to support ongoing health programmes. No response has been provided to date.

a4082.speaker: Senior government official at the Ministry of Health in Osun (anonymous)
a4082.name: Senior government official at the Ministry of Health in Osun (anonymous)
a4082.speech: Said the state government is also trying to raise over a billion naira to bridge the gap that is already becoming obvious. "The TB programme was doing fine, and we were moving towards the point of sustainability with the help of donors. Actually, we've got to the level of epidemic control in TB, but if we don't sustain the successes of the pre-Trump regime, patients will develop drug-resistant TB." ; "We may have a surge. There are some communities that are not easily accessible. We had people who could take drugs to patients at home. We had community testers, officials who stayed in these hard-to-reach areas. But they have been disengaged by partners who hired them."

a4082.speaker: Happy Adedapo, Oyo State chairman of the Nigerian Medical Association (NMA)
a4082.name: Happy Adedapo
a4082.title: Oyo State chairman of the Nigerian Medical Association (NMA)
a4082.speech: Said the withdrawal of foreign funds portends great danger to the Nigerian healthcare system; said blaming a foreign country for withholding its funds is not the way out, but the government must look inwards, cut down on "frivolities and extravagance" to take care of its citizens. "I foresee a crisis of pandemic proportions. I can tell you categorically now that there is a resurgence in the incidence of HIV/AIDs. New cases are being recorded, unlike in the past when people had access to drugs and viral loads were reduced to the barest minimum. But now, these drugs are no longer readily available. The viral loads are increasing, which aids transmission easily." ; "When the political elites are affected by anything, they jump up and ensure their interests are protected. Now that HIV and tuberculosis may not touch them, we have to appeal to them. We knew what happened during the COVID pandemic... the political elites looked inwards. They raised emergency funds and set up emergency centres..." ; "The question to now ask is: where are those emergency and infectious centres set up during the COVID period? They have become moribund. Why should we allow another pandemic to come before we start creating emergency solutions?" ; "There's this saying that adversity may actually bring out the best in you. With the lack of funds from foreign donors, it should be an opportunity to strengthen our capacity. If we put so much into the system, we should expect something good."

a4097.speaker: Convention People’s Party, led by Kwame Nkrumah
a4097.name: Convention People’s Party
a4097.title: led by Kwame Nkrumah
a4097.speech: Campaigned for full independence under the slogan “Self-government now.”

a4137.speaker: David Lammy, British Foreign Minister
a4137.name: David Lammy
a4137.title: British Foreign Minister
a4137.speech: Told parliament on Tuesday Rwanda received over US$1 billion in global aid every year, including around 32 million pounds ($39.80 million) of bilateral UK assistance but “all of that is under threat when you attack your neighbours” ; “We in this House are clear that we cannot have countries challenging the territorial integrity of other countries. Just as we will not tolerate it in the continent of Europe, we cannot tolerate it wherever in the world it happens.”

a4137.speaker: Britain (UK government)
a4137.name: Britain (UK government)
a4137.speech: Has warned Rwanda that its involvement in an escalating conflict in the Democratic Republic of Congo could jeopardise the over US$1 billion of aid it receives every year.

a4137.speaker: Reuters
a4137.name: Reuters
a4137.speech: Cited as the source of the report.

a4244.speaker: Leaked document “Mission – Tanzania 2025 Elections Action Plan”
a4244.name: Leaked document “Mission – Tanzania 2025 Elections Action Plan”
a4244.speech: Alleges that USAID, under the banner of promoting democracy and governance, has allocated funds for political space and support to key opposition figures, including CHADEMA and ACT-Wazalendo's leadership; it also outlines coordination for U.S. election observation, civic education efforts, and potential crisis response planning through the Embassy-led Election Working Group.

a4244.speaker: U.S. Embassy in Dar es Salaam (statement issued Friday)
a4244.name: U.S. Embassy in Dar es Salaam (statement issued Friday)
a4244.speech: “We have determined that these documents are false and do not reflect U.S. Embassy policy vis-à-vis the elections.”

a4244.speaker: Officials from CHADEMA and ACT-Wazalendo
a4244.name: Officials from CHADEMA and ACT-Wazalendo
a4244.speech: Declined to comment, stating they were reviewing the leaked document.

a4244.speaker: Amos Makalla, Secretary for Ideology and Publicity, Chama Cha Mapinduzi (CCM)
a4244.name: Amos Makalla
a4244.title: Secretary for Ideology and Publicity, Chama Cha Mapinduzi (CCM)
a4244.speech: Said the party had received the report and was analyzing it.

a4244.speaker: William Lukuvi, Minister of State in the Prime Minister's Office
a4244.name: William Lukuvi
a4244.title: Minister of State in the Prime Minister's Office
a4244.speech: Said he was not aware of the document but would follow up on its authenticity.

a4244.speaker: Ramadhan Kailima, Director of Elections, Independent National Electoral Commission (INEC)
a4244.name: Ramadhan Kailima
a4244.title: Director of Elections, Independent National Electoral Commission (INEC)
a4244.speech: Distanced the Commission from any alleged external financing of political parties, clarifying that: “INEC does not oversee how political parties acquire their funding or operational resources—this falls under the Office of the Registrar of Political Parties,” he said in a phone interview.

a4244.speaker: Ramadhan Kailima, Director of Elections, Independent National Electoral Commission (INEC)
a4244.name: Ramadhan Kailima
a4244.title: Director of Elections, Independent National Electoral Commission (INEC)
a4244.speech: Confirmed that USAID is among the institutions granted permission to observe the ongoing voter registration process: “We opened applications for civic education and observation permits on April 21, and the deadline is May 20, 2025.”

a4244.speaker: Sisty Nyahoza, Deputy Registrar of Political Parties
a4244.name: Sisty Nyahoza
a4244.title: Deputy Registrar of Political Parties
a4244.speech: When contacted, was not available for comment.

a4244.speaker: Prominent analyst (anonymous, civil society)
a4244.name: Prominent analyst (anonymous
a4244.title: civil society)
a4244.speech: “This is a coordinated attempt to discredit the opposition,” said one prominent analyst who requested anonymity, pointing fingers at CCM; some civil society activists have dismissed the leaked plan as fabricated and politically motivated.

a4244.speaker: Ministry of Foreign Affairs of Tanzania
a4244.name: Ministry of Foreign Affairs of Tanzania
a4244.speech: Has not commented, though efforts are ongoing to obtain its position on the matter.

a4244.speaker: CHADEMA, Tanzania's main opposition party
a4244.name: CHADEMA
a4244.title: Tanzania's main opposition party
a4244.speech: Has distanced itself from running in the forthcoming general election, demanding a deadline extension and adequate reforms, notably of the electoral commission, to facilitate what it called a free and fair election.

a4244.speaker: Government of Tanzania
a4244.name: Government of Tanzania
a4244.speech: Has insisted that key reforms have been made, including establishing an Independent Electoral Commission (INEC).

a4377.speaker: National Agency for Food and Drug Administration and Control (NAFDAC) (statement on its official website)
a4377.name: National Agency for Food and Drug Administration and Control (NAFDAC) (statement on its official website)
a4377.speech: Has raised an alert over “falsified” Type 1 and 2 batches of Postinor 2 (Levonorgestrel 0.75mg) product in circulation in Nigeria; said that it received a report from the Society of Family Health (SFH), the MAH, which confirmed that their company did not import the said fake product batch.

a4377.speaker: Society of Family Health (SFH), Marketing Authorisation Holder (report to NAFDAC)
a4377.name: Society of Family Health (SFH)
a4377.title: Marketing Authorisation Holder (report to NAFDAC)
a4377.speech: Confirmed that their company did not import the said fake product batch.

a4377.speaker: National Agency for Food and Drug Administration and Control (NAFDAC)
a4377.name: National Agency for Food and Drug Administration and Control (NAFDAC)
a4377.speech: Stated that the noticeable difference found between the fake and the original versions of the product showed that the font size of the text on the pin verification sticker of the fake version appears smaller and has a wrong spelling of the word Veify instead of Verify, while the text font on the sticker of the original appears bigger and more visible ; “There is also a wrong spelling behind the pack of the fake distributed in Nigeria instead of distributed in Nigeria,” NAFDAC added.

a4377.speaker: National Agency for Food and Drug Administration and Control (NAFDAC) (risk statement)
a4377.name: National Agency for Food and Drug Administration and Control (NAFDAC) (risk statement)
a4377.speech: Said that due to the potential presence of “incorrect, substandard, or harmful ingredients, improper dosages of levonorgestrel, and a lack of sterile manufacturing conditions, poses significant risks to individual health and public safety” ; noted, “The risks of administering falsified Postinor 2 (Levonorgestrel 0.75mg) include failure of contraceptive effect, toxic or harmful contaminants, unpredictable side effects, delayed or missed opportunity for genuine emergency contraception, and potential long-term reproductive health impact” ; said that unknown substances can trigger allergic reactions, organ damage, or death ; “Counterfeit medicines are unregulated, untested, and illegal, making their safety and efficacy impossible to guarantee. Patients should only obtain Postinor-2 from verified pharmacies or licensed healthcare providers,” the agency said.

a4377.speaker: National Agency for Food and Drug Administration and Control (NAFDAC)
a4377.name: National Agency for Food and Drug Administration and Control (NAFDAC)
a4377.speech: Said that although investigations are still ongoing regarding the source of the falsified product, all its zonal directors and state coordinators have been directed to carry out surveillance and mop up the falsified product of type 1 and 2 Postinor 2 (Levonorgestrel 0.75mg) within the zones and states ; “Distributors, retailers, healthcare professionals, and caregivers are advised to exercise caution and vigilance in the supply chain to prevent the distribution, sale, and use of falsified products. All medical products must be obtained from authorized/licensed suppliers. The products’ authenticity and physical condition should be carefully checked,” NAFDAC added.

a4408.speaker: Minister of Transport and Infrastructure of Mali (communique of 5 February)
a4408.name: Minister of Transport and Infrastructure of Mali (communique of 5 February)
a4408.speech: Urged owners of heavy goods transport vehicles to strictly comply with the standards relating to dimensions, weights and axle load, within the framework of the full application of Article 32 of Decree No. 2023-0509/PT-RM of 12 September 2023.

a4408.speaker: Mamadou Sow, Director General of Transport of Mali
a4408.name: Mamadou Sow
a4408.title: Director General of Transport of Mali
a4408.speech: “Our country is concerned with preserving its road heritage. Every year, the State invests billions of CFA francs in road construction and maintenance. The Road Maintenance Fund collects toll revenues and the usage levy on petroleum products, but these resources are not sufficient to keep in good condition a road network some of whose infrastructure is more than 20 years old. These roads must guarantee a safe service that meets users’ requirements.” ; said the objective of this measure is to prevent the premature degradation of the roads and crossing structures, with maximum authorised dimensions of 16.5 m in length for articulated vehicles, 2.55 m in width and 4 m in height, and sanctions from 1 April 2025 including immobilisation of the vehicle and obligation of transshipment.

a4408.speaker: Mamadou Sow, Director General of Transport of Mali
a4408.name: Mamadou Sow
a4408.title: Director General of Transport of Mali
a4408.speech: “The highway code defines these standards and imposes strict limits on vehicle dimensions. When a truck of 20 to 22 tonnes travels on a road designed to bear 13 tonnes per axle, after only three passages the structure of the area is weakened. The first rain is then enough to create holes, commonly called potholes.” ; “It is 18 tonnes maximum for a single vehicle (truck) with two axles, and 26 tonnes for a three-axle vehicle. It is a maximum of 80 tonnes for articulated vehicles with several axles, a nine-axle double-articulated container road train. These vehicles are not found here. Most often, that is in exceptional transport. And for a vehicle for normal transport, the maximum authorised is 56 tonnes all weights included.” ; insisted that no vehicle must exceed the load limit inscribed on its registration document, in accordance with international regulations ; “It is time that we took care of our investments. Too often, a road begins to deteriorate even before its inauguration. If we do not comply with the standards, we will continue to see our infrastructure deteriorate prematurely.” ; deplored that a vehicle was checked at the Ouessebougou toll post with 36 tonnes per axle, exceeding the authorised maximum of 13 tonnes.

a4408.speaker: Mamadou Sow, Director General of Transport of Mali
a4408.name: Mamadou Sow
a4408.title: Director General of Transport of Mali
a4408.speech: Said the Minister in charge of Transport, Mrs Dembele Madina Sissoko, has approached her counterparts in the transit countries through the Minister of Foreign Affairs and International Cooperation to inform them officially of the measure, and that firm instructions were sent to the directors of the warehouses in the transit ports ; “All the ministers and directors of transport of the AES countries have been informed of this decision.”

a4408.speaker: Mamadou Sow, Director General of Transport of Mali
a4408.name: Mamadou Sow
a4408.title: Director General of Transport of Mali
a4408.speech: “The roads are built by the State and the State is going to ban non-compliant vehicles from travelling on its roads. Those who wish to continue using the Malian road network will be obliged to comply with the standards and dimensions set by the highway code.” ; indicated that monitoring of compliance with the new regulations will be ensured by the competent public services, deployed at tolls, control posts, borders and in the Malian warehouses of the transit ports ; “The State has given itself the necessary means to guarantee the application and follow-up of these measures.” ; “This problem is mainly caused by a minority of vehicle owners who are not professional transporters. They represent only 0.3% of the sector, but their behaviour affects the entire road network.”

a4413.speaker: Sirak Gebrehiwot, UN partnerships and development finance adviser
a4413.name: Sirak Gebrehiwot
a4413.title: UN partnerships and development finance adviser
a4413.speech: Speaking to the Daily News, said this year the UN was focusing on financing developmental projects that ensure sustainability and long-term impact on the country’s economic growth, rather than short-term gains ; “The UN development system in Zimbabwe continues its efforts to support the government by promoting universal health coverage, quality education, and improved water, sanitation, and hygiene (WASH) services. The initiative focuses on social assistance programmes, ending violence against women, sustainable agriculture, food and nutritional security, disaster risk reduction, environmental protection, decent work and employment opportunities, industrialisation, enhanced public service delivery, strengthening institutional capacities, encouraging public participation in decision making, ensuring compliance with international human rights standards, and fostering peace and social cohesion. The estimated budget of the UN Zimbabwe Cooperation Framework for 2025 is US$ 370,7 million this is an estimate which includes a component of available and to be mobilised during the year. We want to ensure support of a number of key projects such as universal health coverage such as access to HIV treatment, Tuberculosis and Malaria.”

a4413.speaker: Sirak Gebrehiwot, UN partnerships and development finance adviser
a4413.name: Sirak Gebrehiwot
a4413.title: UN partnerships and development finance adviser
a4413.speech: Noted that in 2024, 51 percent of the US$317,8 million spent by the UN system was allocated through 10 Joint Programmes, such as the Health Resilience Fund and the Global Partnership for Education ; “These initiatives often rely on global and vertical funding, highlighting the need for increased country-based pooled funding mechanisms, as many current programs are nearing completion.”

a4413.speaker: Sirak Gebrehiwot, UN partnerships and development finance adviser
a4413.name: Sirak Gebrehiwot
a4413.title: UN partnerships and development finance adviser
a4413.speech: “Looking ahead to 2025, the UN system in Zimbabwe plans to transition from a focus on funding to development financing, under the leadership and ownership of the government of Zimbabwe for its national development agenda and the 2030 Agenda for Sustainable Development. We aim to foster a spirit of independence and strengthen Zimbabwe’s capacity. Sustainability is at the heart of our efforts, empowering communities to thrive beyond reliance on non-governmental organisations. Our goal is to nurture local businesses, enabling communities to take ownership of their lives and become self-sufficient. So that is the concept of development financing as opposed to funding a certain project.”

a4414.speaker: Joe Biden, US President
a4414.name: Joe Biden
a4414.title: US President
a4414.speech: Said a ceasefire and hostage release deal he has championed was on “the brink” of coming to fruition ; “The deal ... would free the hostages, halt the fighting, provide security to Israel and allow us to significantly surge humanitarian assistance to the Palestinians who suffered terribly in this war that Hamas started,” he said in a speech on Monday to highlight his foreign policy achievements.

a4414.speaker: An official briefed on the negotiations (anonymous)
a4414.name: An official briefed on the negotiations (anonymous)
a4414.speech: Said mediators gave Israel and Hamas a final draft of a deal on Monday, after a midnight “breakthrough” in talks attended by envoys of both the outgoing US president and President-elect Donald Trump; said the text for a ceasefire and release of hostages was presented by Qatar to both sides at talks in Doha, which included the chiefs of Israel’s Mossad and Shin Bet spy agencies and Qatar’s prime minister.

a4414.speaker: Antony Blinken, US Secretary of State
a4414.name: Antony Blinken
a4414.title: US Secretary of State
a4414.speech: Said the sides were “closer than we’ve ever been” to a deal, and the ball was in Hamas’ court.

a4414.speaker: Hamas
a4414.name: Hamas
a4414.speech: Said it was keen on reaching a deal ; has always insisted a deal must lead to a permanent end to the war and Israeli withdrawal from Gaza.

a4414.speaker: Hamas delegation in Doha (statement)
a4414.name: Hamas delegation in Doha (statement)
a4414.speech: Issued a statement on Monday after a meeting with Qatar’s Emir Sheikh Tamim bin Hamad Al-Thani saying talks were progressing well.

a4414.speaker: An Israeli official (anonymous)
a4414.name: An Israeli official (anonymous)
a4414.speech: Said negotiations were in advanced stages for the release of up to 33 hostages as part of the deal.

a4414.speaker: Israeli authorities
a4414.name: Israeli authorities
a4414.speech: Ninety-eight hostages remain in Gaza, according to Israeli authorities.

a4414.speaker: Israel (government position)
a4414.name: Israel (government position)
a4414.speech: Has said it will not end the war until Hamas is dismantled.

a4414.speaker: Israeli tallies
a4414.name: Israeli tallies
a4414.speech: Hamas fighters stormed across Israel’s borders in October 2023, killing 1,200 people and taking more than 250 hostages, according to Israeli tallies.

a4414.speaker: Palestinian health officials
a4414.name: Palestinian health officials
a4414.speech: More than 46,000 people have been killed in Gaza, according to Palestinian health officials.

a4452.speaker: Gautam I Menon, professor, Departments of Physics and Biology, Ashoka University
a4452.name: Gautam I Menon
a4452.title: professor, Departments of Physics and Biology, Ashoka University
a4452.speech: Told PTI: "A dwindling fraction of these cases will be severe enough to lead to death. It is this new normal that we must become accustomed to." ; “The world cannot function in a state of permanent heightened alertness.” ; "This is certainly an indicator that a major phase of the current pandemic is now ending, although we should be careful how we interpret the word 'ending'."

a4452.speaker: Gautam I Menon, professor, Departments of Physics and Biology, Ashoka University
a4452.name: Gautam I Menon
a4452.title: professor, Departments of Physics and Biology, Ashoka University
a4452.speech: Said we might well hope that we are emerging from the shadow of the COVID-19 pandemic, provided a more transmissible as well as more virulent variant strain does not appear; and that going forward the decisions on what steps need to be taken to protect oneself can now be left to the individual, with no need for further state intervention, especially in a punitive way.

a4452.speaker: World Health Organization (WHO)
a4452.name: World Health Organization (WHO)
a4452.speech: Is now expressing optimism that the end of the COVID-19 pandemic is in sight.

a4452.speaker: Tedros Adhanom Ghebreyesus, WHO Director-General
a4452.name: Tedros Adhanom Ghebreyesus
a4452.title: WHO Director-General
a4452.speech: Said on the sidelines of the UN General Assembly: "We have spent two-and-a-half years in a long, dark tunnel, and we are just beginning to glimpse the light at the end of that tunnel" ; "But it is still a long way off, and the tunnel is still dark, with many obstacles that could trip us up if we don't take care." ; said at a press conference last week that the world has never been in a better position to end the pandemic: “We are not there yet, but the end is in sight.”

a4452.speaker: World Health Organization (WHO)
a4452.name: World Health Organization (WHO)
a4452.speech: Cautioned that coronavirus still poses an “acute global emergency” and highlighted that during the first eight months of 2022 more than one million people died from COVID-19; affirmed that countries need to take a hard look at their policies and strengthen them for COVID-19 and future viruses, urging nations to vaccinate 100 per cent of their high-risk groups and keep testing for the virus.

a4452.speaker: Ramanan Laxminarayan, epidemiologist, director of the Center for Disease Dynamics, Economics & Policy (CDDEP), Washington
a4452.name: Ramanan Laxminarayan
a4452.title: epidemiologist, director of the Center for Disease Dynamics, Economics & Policy (CDDEP), Washington
a4452.speech: Agreed, saying Covid risk is lower as long as individuals are vaccinated so they should no longer worry about the pandemic as far as their health is concerned. Told PTI: "Due to vaccination and widespread population exposure, the risk of hospitalisation and death has come down a lot so in the sense of the public attention moving on, it is only to be expected." ; said that since testing has moved away from labs to the home, case numbers being reported may give a false sense that the pandemic is over, adding "But the bottom line is that we should get vaccinated and stop worrying." ; said the message for policymakers should be to continue to focus on Covid vaccination while that for the general public must be to not worry as long as they are vaccinated: "Although the Covid disease is not going to disappear, it is unlikely that we will see a big resurgence in Covid deaths and hospitalisations if we go back to life as normal. A new strain that is dangerous could always emerge but we can then take appropriate measures at that time."

a4452.speaker: Sanjeev Galande, cell biologist, dean, School of Natural Sciences, Shiv Nadar Institution of Eminence
a4452.name: Sanjeev Galande
a4452.title: cell biologist, dean, School of Natural Sciences, Shiv Nadar Institution of Eminence
a4452.speech: Noted that the pandemic is showing signs of ending soon but the coronavirus may remain with us for a much longer time. Told PTI: "If we look at the trend since the beginning of 2022, overall cases, hospitalisations and deaths in most countries - though not all - are rapidly decreasing." ; noted there is growing evidence that the SARS-CoV-2 virus will eventually turn seasonal, a characteristic of several other respiratory illnesses ; said of the hospitalised death rate: "It was about 15 per cent during the predominance of the Delta variant and has dropped steadily over the last year to less than 3 per cent during the late Omicron phase, which is good news!"

a4452.speaker: US Center for Disease Control and Prevention (CDC)
a4452.name: US Center for Disease Control and Prevention (CDC)
a4452.speech: According to the CDC, the rate of death for those sick enough to be hospitalised has decreased dramatically.

a4452.speaker: WHO Coronavirus dashboard (data)
a4452.name: WHO Coronavirus dashboard (data)
a4452.speech: According to the dashboard, on September 22 the number of daily reported global deaths stood at 1,395, the lowest since March 2020, while the number of new cases was 428,321, the lowest since October 2020; globally, as of September 22, 2022, there have been 610,866,075 confirmed cases of COVID-19, including 6,510,139 deaths reported to WHO, and as of September 19, 2022, a total of 12,640,866,343 vaccine doses have been administered.

a4452.speaker: Several scientists (collectively)
a4452.name: Several scientists (collectively)
a4452.speech: Say the worst of COVID-19 is over, perhaps for the first time in more than two years; said the pandemic will be over but COVID-19 will be here to stay, and that the worst may be over but it may be quite a while before we declare the end of the pandemic.

a4498.speaker: Ministry of Education of Cabo Verde (Caderno de Orientações / statement)
a4498.name: Ministry of Education of Cabo Verde (Caderno de Orientações / statement)
a4498.speech: According to the ministry, this decision aims to reduce distractions during classes, encourage concentration, foster healthy interaction among students and prevent the inappropriate use of mobile devices; among the risks identified are access to inappropriate content and cyberbullying. The Ministry of Education clarifies that mobile phones may be used as a pedagogical support tool, provided this is under the guidance and supervision of teachers and integrated into teaching-and-learning strategies.

a4498.speaker: Ministry of Education of Cabo Verde (statement)
a4498.name: Ministry of Education of Cabo Verde (statement)
a4498.speech: In the statement, the ME notes that the measure follows a trend already adopted in other countries such as Portugal, France, the United States, South Korea and Japan ; The ME states that greater dynamism and discipline were observed, both inside and outside the classroom, as well as an increase in interaction among students, in the experience at Liceu Abílio Duarte in Praia.

a4498.speaker: Studies by the Centre for Planning and Evaluation of Public Policies (Portugal)
a4498.name: Studies by the Centre for Planning and Evaluation of Public Policies (Portugal)
a4498.speech: Reveal that limiting the use of mobile phones in schools is associated with a reduction in bullying, indiscipline and conflict, as well as an increase in socialisation among students, physical activity and time spent in libraries.

a4664.speaker: Abari Lawan Marouma, civil society actor and chairman of the board of the NGO PLADIA
a4664.name: Abari Lawan Marouma
a4664.title: civil society actor and chairman of the board of the NGO PLADIA
a4664.speech: Said that “it is thousands of tonnes of salt and natron that are exploited by the communities”; cited “natron at a village called Achounouma in the locality of Dirkou... there are two types of natron that are exploited, including black natron, called borno, which is used in making skin-lightening cosmetic products destined for export to Nigeria and Ghana” ; “red natron, which is known to Nigeriens because it is used in food and in other medical treatments” ; Bilma and Fachi are known for “the exploitation of white salt, which is called cooking salt, and black salt, which is used by livestock herders, and it is thousands of tonnes that the population produces each year” ; “These products are Nigerien products that are used in the consumption of human food, and of livestock feed as well.”

a4664.speaker: Abari Lawan Marouma, civil society actor and chairman of the board of the NGO PLADIA
a4664.name: Abari Lawan Marouma
a4664.title: civil society actor and chairman of the board of the NGO PLADIA
a4664.speech: Called on the State for support: “we expect the State to take action to boost the economy in terms of irrigation and support to farmers in cereal production”; asked the State and its partners “to support these value chains, because they are promising value chains” ; suggested “Many cosmetic products, and detergents such as Omo, are made from black natron; we could develop a small local industry that would allow them to be produced here instead of importing them”, wishing that “this sector be promoted; there is not much publicity or promotional activity for these products, because what we lack is, first of all, production on an artisanal basis” ; said Kawar Week allows Nigeriens to know that “these products are from Kawar.”

a4664.speaker: Ramadan Moussa, native of Kawar exhibiting natron at Kawar Week
a4664.name: Ramadan Moussa
a4664.title: native of Kawar exhibiting natron at Kawar Week
a4664.speech: Explained that “red natron originates from Achinouma in the commune of Dirkou; it is used in cooking, in digestive therapy and in cosmetics, and also against stomach aches”, while brown natron originates from Bilma and is used in dyeing.

a4664.speaker: Moussa Boukar Chégou, participant in Kawar Week
a4664.name: Moussa Boukar Chégou
a4664.title: participant in Kawar Week
a4664.speech: Declared: “We are here as part of the exhibition of our local products such as the Balma, which is a salt for cooking, of good quality and above all iodised; it does not cause goitre, very delicious for sauce”, specifying that “the salt with the brown colour is destined for livestock; it gives them appetite and strength, and it is recommended during the rainy season.”

a4664.speaker: Elhaji Lawan Taher, date producer from Kawar
a4664.name: Elhaji Lawan Taher
a4664.title: date producer from Kawar
a4664.speech: Noted that “Kawar is also known for its high-quality dates produced from 20,000 to 30,000 date palms”, adding that “these are dates of several generations, which we inherited from our parents and our grandparents, from 50, 60 years ago” ; expressed the need for support from partners and the State, because “it rains less in the localities of Kawar; 20mm per year is insufficient for the production of good dates, we have an urgent need for water” ; “We will need projects of national scope to further improve the dates, because it is with dates that one makes jams, certain biscuits and many other things” ; called on the State of Niger to “help date producers in quality and in quantity, help them to obtain vehicles to freeze the harvests all the way to the cities in order to sell them, and to build many more water boreholes.”

a4664.speaker: Mr. Ari, native of Kawar
a4664.name: Mr. Ari
a4664.title: native of Kawar
a4664.speech: Cites some varieties of dates including “the Karab, a variety of date produced in all the communes of Kawar; the Soubour, a variety appreciated for its sweet flavour; the Youlfodom, known for its quality and delicious taste; Korossom, known for its quality and taste, produced notably in Fachi; the Aguissune, a variety cultivated in the oases of Kawar; and the Dilo, appreciated for its texture and taste.”

a4844.speaker: Financial Afrik (Guinea-Bissau/regional media report)
a4844.name: Financial Afrik (Guinea-Bissau/regional media report)
a4844.speech: Reported that Umaro Sissoco Embaló inaugurated on Monday 16 June the country's first motorway, a 14-kilometre stretch linking Osvaldo Vieira International Airport to the town of Safim, and that this China-financed modern infrastructure marks a major step forward since the country's independence in 1973.

a4844.speaker: Republic of Togo (state media/official announcement)
a4844.name: Republic of Togo (state media/official announcement)
a4844.speech: Announced that more than 100,000 candidates have registered for the 2025 baccalaureate, an increase of 29.55%, a figure reflecting growing enthusiasm for the qualification, which is seen as a springboard to higher education and working life.

a4844.speaker: Graphic (Ghanaian newspaper), citing a notice from the University of Ghana Registrar's Office dated 16 June 2025
a4844.name: Graphic (Ghanaian newspaper)
a4844.title: citing a notice from the University of Ghana Registrar's Office dated 16 June 2025
a4844.speech: Reported that 115 students of the University of Ghana were sanctioned for misconduct and examination malpractice, with sanctions ranging from expulsion to reprimand, including suspensions and grade penalties.

a4844.speaker: Dennis Dominic Adjei, Judge and candidate for Ghana's Supreme Court
a4844.name: Dennis Dominic Adjei
a4844.title: Judge and candidate for Ghana's Supreme Court
a4844.speech: Defended maintaining the traditional dress of legal practitioners, holding that wigs and gowns preserve the dignity, identity and security of the judicial system.

a4844.speaker: Premium Times (Nigerian newspaper)
a4844.name: Premium Times (Nigerian newspaper)
a4844.speech: Reported that more than 6,000 people were displaced in recent attacks in Benue State.

a4844.speaker: National Emergency Management Agency (NEMA), Nigeria
a4844.name: National Emergency Management Agency (NEMA)
a4844.title: Nigeria
a4844.speech: Reported that more than 3,000 of the displaced, including many children and women, require urgent humanitarian assistance.

a4844.speaker: Punch NG (Nigerian newspaper)
a4844.name: Punch NG (Nigerian newspaper)
a4844.speech: Held that these events amount to a "bloodbath" at Yelewata, in the Guma local government area, where some 200 villagers were reportedly killed on the night of 13 June, and that a cross-border manhunt has been launched by the army and the police to find the perpetrators.

a4844.speaker: Premium Times (editorial)
a4844.name: Premium Times (editorial)
a4844.speech: Denounced property-tax fraud by the Abuja elite.

a4844.speaker: Nyesom Wike, Minister of the Federal Capital Territory (FCT), Nigeria
a4844.name: Nyesom Wike
a4844.title: Minister of the Federal Capital Territory (FCT), Nigeria
a4844.speech: Pointed to the elite's aversion to paying property taxes, the main source of uncollected revenue since he took office.

a4844.speaker: Mountaga Tall, Malian opposition figure
a4844.name: Mountaga Tall
a4844.title: Malian opposition figure
a4844.speech: Called on the transitional president, General Assimi Goïta, to give up the five-year mandate recently envisaged to extend the transition under way since 2021 ; argued for an inclusive dialogue, the restoration of political parties and the reopening of dissolved civil society organisations.

a4844.speaker: Le Soleil (Senegalese newspaper)
a4844.name: Le Soleil (Senegalese newspaper)
a4844.speech: Announced the forthcoming publication of quarterly budget execution reports by the Ministry of Finance and Budget, to be available on Monday 23 June after a change of approach that caused a slight delay.

a5111.speaker: Kenyan khat farmers
a5111.name: Kenyan khat farmers
a5111.speech: Frustrated with what they describe as exploitative pricing, demand that exporters pay an additional 300 Kenyan shillings (Ksh) per kilogram and enforce a minimum payment of Ksh 200,000 per bag for the premium "Grid" variety of khat ; argue they receive Ksh 300 - an imbalance they say enriches intermediaries and transporters at their expense ; have vowed to continue their protest, even as negotiations unfold.

a5111.speaker: Kenyan khat farmers
a5111.name: Kenyan khat farmers
a5111.speech: Point to an illegal levy of USD 4.5 per kilogram allegedly imposed by a "cartel" at Jomo Kenyatta International Airport (JKIA); they claim this hidden cost is undermining farm-gate prices while inflating Mogadishu's retail rates.

a5111.speaker: Somali traders
a5111.name: Somali traders
a5111.speech: Accuse the government of maintaining policies that favour select importers while leaving local sellers to grapple with soaring costs.

a5111.speaker: Somali female traders
a5111.name: Somali female traders
a5111.speech: In mid-January staged protests in Mogadishu against high taxation on Kenyan khat, claiming it was eroding their profits.

a5111.speaker: Kenya's Agriculture and Food Authority (AFA)
a5111.name: Kenya's Agriculture and Food Authority (AFA)
a5111.speech: Has acknowledged the farmers' grievances; the agency's Khat Pricing Committee has met with industry stakeholders and is weighing a revised pricing framework.

a5111.speaker: James Mithika, Chairman of the Khat Pricing Committee
a5111.name: James Mithika
a5111.title: Chairman of the Khat Pricing Committee
a5111.speech: Confirmed that discussions include the introduction of a guaranteed minimum price of Ksh 700 per kilogram in the dry season and Ksh 500 per kilogram in the rainy season.

a5493.speaker: Bank of Ghana (BoG), notice of August 20, 2025 signed by Aimee V. Quashie for the Secretary
a5493.name: Bank of Ghana (BoG)
a5493.title: notice of August 20, 2025 signed by Aimee V. Quashie for the Secretary
a5493.speech: Expressed concern over the growing practice of foreign currency (FCY) cash withdrawals by bulk oil distribution companies, mining firms and similar large institutions, which it said was exerting "avoidable pressure" on the foreign exchange market and threatening stability ; "Accordingly, with immediate effect, all banks are directed to discontinue the payment of FCY cash to Large Corporates unless such transactions are fully supported by equivalent FCY cash deposits lodged by the same institution" ; explained that banks must retain proper documentation for every pay-out to ensure transparency and traceability of funds, warning that any breaches of the directive will attract regulatory sanctions.

a5493.speaker: Bank of Ghana (BoG)
a5493.name: Bank of Ghana (BoG)
a5493.speech: Underscored the importance of large Corporates to the economy, particularly in petroleum supply, mineral exports, and other critical sectors; said it had partnered with the government to establish mechanisms to provide foreign exchange liquidity for legitimate import obligations ; "These measures are designed to safeguard market stability while ensuring that vital supply chains remain uninterrupted" ; called on all relevant industry associations to ensure that their members strictly comply with the directive.

a5635.speaker: Helder Alberto, director of the district services for economic activities in the Chibabava district of Sofala
a5635.name: Helder Alberto
a5635.title: director of the district services for economic activities in the Chibabava district of Sofala
a5635.speech: Said: ‘At the moment, we have around 32,000 families in a situation of food insecurity who live on remittances and the sale of small animals. The most affected area is the Goonda administrative post, which is our granary in cereal production’ ; According to Alberto, the local government has assisted around 4,100 families affected by the drought, especially those in the Goonda administrative post in the Chibabava district.

a5635.speaker: United Nations Children’s Fund (UNICEF) (statement)
a5635.name: United Nations Children’s Fund (UNICEF) (statement)
a5635.speech: Recently estimated that around 4.8 million people need humanitarian assistance in Mozambique, with $64 million (€60.6 million) needed to meet the needs ; ‘The poly-crisis in Mozambique—conflict, drought and public health emergencies—are stretching humanitarian resources. Approximately 4.8 million people require humanitarian assistance (10 per cent persons with disabilities), including 3.4 million children.’

a5635.speaker: United Nations (UN)
a5635.name: United Nations (UN)
a5635.speech: In September 2024, said that nearly two million people needed humanitarian assistance in the country ; explained: ‘This year, Mozambique was affected by drought induced by the El Niño phenomenon during the 2023-2024 season. It is estimated that around 1.8 million people could face food insecurity between October and March 2025. Faced with this situation, the need for humanitarian assistance for the affected communities has been increasing, especially in Mozambique’s central and southern regions.’

a5678.speaker: Mohamud Ma’allin Abdulle, Commissioner of the Somali Disaster Management Authority (SODMA)
a5678.name: Mohamud Ma’allin Abdulle
a5678.title: Commissioner of the Somali Disaster Management Authority (SODMA)
a5678.speech: Expressed profound gratitude to the United States Government for its support, particularly through the United States Agency for International Development (USAID); acknowledged the critical role of USAID in facilitating aid and development efforts in Somalia.

a5753.speaker: 2007 Health Policy Statement (Tamko la Sera ya Afya ya Mwaka 2007)
a5753.name: 2007 Health Policy Statement (Tamko la Sera ya Afya ya Mwaka 2007)
a5753.speech: Requires that there be sufficient skilled staff in various professions at all levels of service delivery in the country.

a5753.speaker: Dr Mugisha Nkoronko, President of the Medical Association of Tanzania (MAT)
a5753.name: Dr Mugisha Nkoronko
a5753.title: President of the Medical Association of Tanzania (MAT)
a5753.speech: Said that knowing the fate of health facilities, health workers and the assurance of medicines is the biggest issue, especially at this time when USAID funding has gone: "We are all eagerly waiting to hear the plans. We think the budget will fill the budget deficit after America reduced aid; many expect to see plans that will let them see the future of their health" ; said Tanzanians want to see strategies for controlling epidemic diseases, non-communicable diseases and accidents.

a5753.speaker: Dr Ali Mzige, public health expert
a5753.name: Dr Ali Mzige
a5753.title: public health expert
a5753.speech: Said he is not sure whether the Ministry of Health's budget has reached 15 percent of Government spending, as required since the Abuja agreement that a country should spend at least 15 percent of its revenue on health; secondly said development must always target the population segment that is most affected: "For example small children under five years and pregnant women; there is still a problem in areas that grow food in abundance, but still have stunted children. If you take areas like Katavi, Njombe, Iringa, much of the food grown is sold but stunting is high; it should have been directed to the community" ; said it is important to tell mothers and fathers about children's health and the importance of eating leafy vegetables and fruits, and to remind the community to clean their mouths twice a day and avoid smoking, with that education starting in schools.

a5753.speaker: Another health-sector stakeholder who did not want his name mentioned / one of the workers in public hospitals (anonymous)
a5753.name: Another health-sector stakeholder who did not want his name mentioned / one of the workers in public hospitals (anonymous)
a5753.speech: Said health insurance had not been well planned from the time it started because it focused more on treatment and not on prevention: "If there is a disease that has high costs it is kidney dialysis, diabetes and blood pressure; beneficiaries are not educated on what to do, they come when they have already fallen ill" ; "The budget has never allocated for the presence of these specialists in district areas; there is no balance between Tamisemi and the Ministry of Health; a patient has to travel 90 kilometres to the region and if he is overwhelmed he dies on the way before reaching the hospital." ; "Ambulances carry many patients, they use fuel and they are bought expensively; if you look at a driver's salary and the high cost of fuel, the money exceeds what it would take to employ a specialist doctor in the district."

a5753.speaker: Hafidh Omary, resident of Tegeta, Dar es Salaam
a5753.name: Hafidh Omary
a5753.title: resident of Tegeta, Dar es Salaam
a5753.speech: Said the Government has made purchases of equipment that are many, countless and without good direction: "An MRI sells for two billion; you could employ 199 doctors for a year and pay them well. Equipment and a person are two different things; you cannot provide a car without a driver."

a5753.speaker: Hawa Mwinjuma, trader at the Feri fish market in Dar es Salaam
a5753.name: Hawa Mwinjuma
a5753.title: trader at the Feri fish market in Dar es Salaam
a5753.speech: Said the problem of accidents in the country is big so the budget must look at ways to reduce them, while criticising the country for growing more tobacco, which has harmful effects: "In Tanzania we lead in growing tobacco; I think while other ministries count it as bringing in income, let us look at how patients are increasing. Also, we mothers should be provided with essential services there in our village in Mtwara; there the situation is not good, we do not even have a specialist doctor for women's diseases, you have to travel far to find one."

a5958.speaker: Lamine Fofana, independent political analyst (op-ed)
a5958.name: Lamine Fofana
a5958.title: independent political analyst (op-ed)
a5958.speech: Argues that France, in an effort to regain its place in Central and West Africa, is actively developing soft power through the financing of NGOs, and that in the Central African Republic French NGOs are becoming an instrument not only of humanitarian aid but also of political manipulation; cites the PISCCA programme financed by the French embassy in Cameroon (400,000 euros in 2019-2020) and the French Development Agency’s DEFI project supporting eight human rights groups since 2014, saying these programmes are often controlled by outside forces and that the emphasis on networking “could imply the formation of loyal structures capable of promoting French interests under cover of human rights work.”

a5958.speaker: Anonymous source at the French embassy in the Central African Republic
a5958.name: Anonymous source at the French embassy in the Central African Republic
a5958.speech: Said the French Ministry of Foreign Affairs asked the embassy to intensify its work with the local population by organising various activities and supporting French NGOs, and that the campaign was deployed in ten countries.

a5958.speaker: Lamine Fofana, independent political analyst (op-ed)
a5958.name: Lamine Fofana
a5958.title: independent political analyst (op-ed)
a5958.speech: Writes that in 2024 France began actively “gathering intelligence” in the CAR and that two France24 journalists, Caroline Dumay and James Stefan Carstens, were arrested in Bangassou for trying to manipulate public opinion, arriving with pre-prepared scenarios involving disinformation against the Central African authorities and seeking testimony from disarmed militiamen and recordings calling for the continuation of the conflict; concludes that France’s soft power in the CAR “is not so much support and assistance as a tool of manipulation and control,” and that France risks losing its credibility and creating the conditions for new conflicts.

a6006.speaker: Lazarus Chakwera, President of Malawi
a6006.name: Lazarus Chakwera
a6006.title: President of Malawi
a6006.speech: Has expressed deep appreciation for the strong bilateral relationship between Malawi and India, in a meeting with Indian President Droupadi Murmu at Kamuzu Palace.

a6006.speaker: Nancy Tembo, Minister of Foreign Affairs
a6006.name: Nancy Tembo
a6006.title: Minister of Foreign Affairs
a6006.speech: Updated the media post-meeting, highlighting President Chakwera's gratitude for India's steadfast support across various sectors, including trade, health, education, and military peacekeeping, and noting that he also acknowledged India's recent humanitarian assistance ; "The President is particularly pleased that the Indian President chose Malawi as one of her official visit destinations." ; "He emphasized India's role in supporting least developed countries in multilateral organizations, ensuring they receive fair treatment on the global stage."

a6007.speaker: Jean-Baptiste Satchivi, President of the Chamber of Commerce and Industry of Benin (CCIB)
a6007.name: Jean-Baptiste Satchivi
a6007.title: President of the Chamber of Commerce and Industry of Benin (CCIB)
a6007.speech: On the signing of the 2nd MCA Compact: "I would like first to say that this signing is a complete success. The work that was done must be commended and I congratulate the President of the Republic for his leadership... We must commend the work of the MCC team and of the MCA-Benin team, on which the Chamber of Commerce and Industry of Benin is represented." ; said the second compact is only the continuation of the first, which was built around port infrastructure - goods flow went from 5 million to 10 million tonnes per year - and produced justice, land and financial-services reforms, while the second compact is focused essentially on the energy sector and on bringing the Beninese and international private sector into production.

a6007.speaker: Jean-Baptiste Satchivi, President of the Chamber of Commerce and Industry of Benin (CCIB)
a6007.name: Jean-Baptiste Satchivi
a6007.title: President of the Chamber of Commerce and Industry of Benin (CCIB)
a6007.speech: On the compact's leverage: said the compact amounts to about 411 million dollars and these resources will produce 78 MW of electrical energy; explained that a cost-sharing fund is provided for within it, so that a private operator who invests in energy for his own consumption and feeds the surplus into the distribution network will receive MCA support in addition, which serves as a catalyst for other investments.

a6007.speaker: Patrice Talon, President of the Republic of Benin (as cited by Satchivi)
a6007.name: Patrice Talon
a6007.title: President of the Republic of Benin (as cited by Satchivi)
a6007.speech: Says that in view of Benin's needs projected over time, the country must achieve 1,000 MW.

a6007.speaker: Jean-Baptiste Satchivi, President of the Chamber of Commerce and Industry of Benin (CCIB)
a6007.name: Jean-Baptiste Satchivi
a6007.title: President of the Chamber of Commerce and Industry of Benin (CCIB)
a6007.speech: On partnership with the American business world: said discussions had begun with the officials of the US Chamber of Commerce's Africa department, leading to the discovery of CIP, a structure supporting the international development of businesses, with which the CCIB plans to sign a partnership shortly; "We must strengthen our work with the United States. The weakness of francophone countries is that we do not have strong economic trade links with the United States. The United States Chamber of Commerce can serve as a support point for strengthening this emerging Africa. We must work to improve our standards in terms of entrepreneurship, to develop our companies so as to be competitive internationally."

a6007.speaker: Jean-Baptiste Satchivi, President of the Chamber of Commerce and Industry of Benin (CCIB)
a6007.name: Jean-Baptiste Satchivi
a6007.title: President of the Chamber of Commerce and Industry of Benin (CCIB)
a6007.speech: On AGOA: said AGOA is a law that opens the American market to nearly 6,000 African products and that the Chamber's new team's first approach is to diagnose its results; noted that only Natura, which produces shea-butter cosmetics, has stayed the course, while textiles have failed because the American market demands mass production and volume; "Fifteen years are in fact not enough to bring oneself up to American standards, to enter the Anglo-Saxon mindset of entrepreneurship." ; "We have many riches that AGOA can awaken but we must be in line with American standards."

a6007.speaker: Jean-Baptiste Satchivi, President of the Chamber of Commerce and Industry of Benin (CCIB)
a6007.name: Jean-Baptiste Satchivi
a6007.title: President of the Chamber of Commerce and Industry of Benin (CCIB)
a6007.speech: On public-private partnership: commended the dialogue begun in October 2012 but said it did not reach its conclusion because of exclusion; said the general assemblies produced a platform bringing everyone together without exclusion whose proceedings will soon be presented to the President of the Republic, that the PPP legal framework is now before Parliament, and that an operational justice system must reassure national and foreign investors.

a6007.speaker: Jean-Baptiste Satchivi, President of the Chamber of Commerce and Industry of Benin (CCIB)
a6007.name: Jean-Baptiste Satchivi
a6007.title: President of the Chamber of Commerce and Industry of Benin (CCIB)
a6007.speech: On the business climate: "What we expect from the government is very simple. First, more consideration towards the one who undertakes, I mean the business leader, whatever their size... We are not going to ask for exemptions on everything from a State that needs a tax budget in order to work." ; said the only thing lacking today is a fruitful dialogue between the public sector and a non-exclusive private-sector platform, and appealed to the President of the Republic to ensure that this platform becomes a reality before his departure, as an important element of his legacy.

a6025.speaker: Hassan Sheikh Mohamud, President of the Federal Republic of Somalia
a6025.name: Hassan Sheikh Mohamud
a6025.title: President of the Federal Republic of Somalia
a6025.speech: "Somalia has come a long way to be one of the members of the EAC. After more than ten years, Somalia now celebrates its role in developing its economy and engaging with other member states" ; "The 2060 Vision of Somalia is a signpost for the Somali people."

a6025.speaker: Hassan Sheikh Mohamud, President of the Federal Republic of Somalia
a6025.name: Hassan Sheikh Mohamud
a6025.title: President of the Federal Republic of Somalia
a6025.speech: Added that Somalia has adopted a private-driven economic system to enhance all sectors of the economy and highlighted the importance of technology: "Artificial intelligence is not the future — it is already here, and if used correctly, it can guide us toward progress."

a6025.speaker: Hassan Sheikh Mohamud, President of the Federal Republic of Somalia
a6025.name: Hassan Sheikh Mohamud
a6025.title: President of the Federal Republic of Somalia
a6025.speech: On education, emphasized: "Education without financial support cannot be achieved. Our universities must begin teaching Arabic, as Somalia has joined the Arab League, and Swahili, as we are now part of the East African Community."

a6025.speaker: Dr. Maxamed Maxamuud Maxamed, Rector of the Somali National University and Chairperson of the EACON 2025 Organizing Committee
a6025.name: Dr. Maxamed Maxamuud Maxamed
a6025.title: Rector of the Somali National University and Chairperson of the EACON 2025 Organizing Committee
a6025.speech: Welcomed participants and underscored the importance of regional collaboration for sustainable development ; reiterated that EACON 2025 provides a platform for dialogue on accelerating economic integration, strengthening trade, and promoting political cooperation across East Africa.

a6025.speaker: Ali Mohamed Omar (Ali Balcad), State Minister for Foreign Affairs of Somalia
a6025.name: Ali Mohamed Omar (Ali Balcad)
a6025.title: State Minister for Foreign Affairs of Somalia
a6025.speech: Noted that the conference focuses on knowledge sharing, agricultural productivity, and leveraging modern technology, expressing optimism that it will produce tangible results.

a6025.speaker: Farah Sheikh Abdikadir, Minister of Education of Somalia
a6025.name: Farah Sheikh Abdikadir
a6025.title: Minister of Education of Somalia
a6025.speech: Highlighted the need for education to guide production and innovation, ensuring strong links between education, trade, and agriculture across the region.

a6025.speaker: Mohamed Abdi Hayir Maareeye, Minister of Agriculture of Somalia
a6025.name: Mohamed Abdi Hayir Maareeye
a6025.title: Minister of Agriculture of Somalia
a6025.speech: "For a long time, our people depended on imported goods, but now, with increased domestic production, we are exporting Somali crops to the world. This is a key priority for boosting the economies of EAC member states."

a6025.speaker: Dr. Mathew
a6025.name: Dr. Mathew
a6025.speech: Emphasized that regional communities have multiple avenues to benefit, making development and everyday life easier and more productive.

a6025.speaker: Kamaal Guutaale, Permanent Secretary in the Prime Minister's Office
a6025.name: Kamaal Guutaale
a6025.title: Permanent Secretary in the Prime Minister's Office
a6025.speech: Said Somalia is investing in economic infrastructure and that educational institutions play a central role in EAC cooperation.

a6025.speaker: Dr. Cabdikariin Muxudiin Axmed, Rector of SIMAD University
a6025.name: Dr. Cabdikariin Muxudiin Axmed
a6025.title: Rector of SIMAD University
a6025.speech: Welcomed Somalia's integration into the regional market, describing it as a milestone for the country.

a6025.speaker: Björn Richter, representing the German Development Agency
a6025.name: Björn Richter
a6025.title: representing the German Development Agency
a6025.speech: Reaffirmed Germany's support: "Somalia is making remarkable strides, having recently joined the East African Community. We are ready to stand with Somalia."

a6030.speaker: Bloomberg (data report)
a6030.name: Bloomberg (data report)
a6030.speech: Data out this week showed that China's exports to the United States plunged by 34.4 percent last month, the sharpest drop since the Covid-19 pandemic, according to Bloomberg.

a6030.speaker: Keyu Jin, Hong Kong University of Science and Technology (in the Financial Times)
a6030.name: Keyu Jin
a6030.title: Hong Kong University of Science and Technology (in the Financial Times)
a6030.speech: "The bulk of consumer credit goes to people under 35" ; "With one click on Alibaba, you can borrow to buy a lipstick."

a6030.speaker: Boston Consulting Group
a6030.name: Boston Consulting Group
a6030.speech: Estimates that by 2030, more than 500 million Chinese will belong to the middle and upper classes.

a6030.speaker: Absolute Strategy Research
a6030.name: Absolute Strategy Research
a6030.speech: Research done by Absolute Strategy Research shows that households have now largely filled the hole in their balance sheets caused by the tanking property market, allowing them more room to spend.

a6030.speaker: Deutsche Bank (survey)
a6030.name: Deutsche Bank (survey)
a6030.speech: A recent Deutsche Bank survey showed 52 percent of respondents were ready to increase discretionary spending, the highest in a year.

a6030.speaker: David Goodman, director of the China Studies Centre at the University of Sydney (quoted in the Financial Times)
a6030.name: David Goodman
a6030.title: director of the China Studies Centre at the University of Sydney (quoted in the Financial Times)
a6030.speech: "Beijing has time and again demonstrated the ability to do the unexpected to reach its longer-term goals."

a6037.speaker: Medical interns (petition)
a6037.name: Medical interns (petition)
a6037.speech: Presented a petition demanding fair pay, clear and consistent policies aligned with labour laws, recognition of their vital role in the healthcare sector, and the provision of medical aid benefits.

a6037.speaker: Community members in Opuwo
a6037.name: Community members in Opuwo
a6037.speech: Say the hospital has become a haven for stray cats and rats, to the point where they invade patients' rooms to prey on their food.

a6037.speaker: Ben Nangombe, Executive Director of the Ministry of Health and Social Services
a6037.name: Ben Nangombe
a6037.title: Executive Director of the Ministry of Health and Social Services
a6037.speech: Urged nurses to carry out their work with love, diligence, and care, during an early International Nurses Day celebration in the capital.

a6037.speaker: Ben Nangombe, Executive Director of the Ministry of Health and Social Services
a6037.name: Ben Nangombe
a6037.title: Executive Director of the Ministry of Health and Social Services
a6037.speech: Urged the public not to panic because of the high number of COVID-19 cases reported in Rehoboth.

a6037.speaker: Executive Director of the Ministry of Health and Social Services (MoHSS)
a6037.name: Executive Director of the Ministry of Health and Social Services (MoHSS)
