a6037.speech: Says the health and well-being of livestock and animals are of paramount importance.

a6167.speaker: Tanzania Trade Development Authority (Tantrade)
a6167.name: Tanzania Trade Development Authority (Tantrade)
a6167.speech: Has announced that more than 70 business people have registered for Expo 2025 in Osaka, Japan.

a6167.speaker: Deo Shayo, Tantrade Senior Business Officer
a6167.name: Deo Shayo
a6167.title: Tantrade Senior Business Officer
a6167.speech: Confirmed that registration numbers are increasing daily, with businesses signing up online for different sessions and programmes ; emphasised that Tanzania’s participation aims to promote its abundant resources, strengthen global economic ties and attract investment ; noted that Expo 2025 will serve as a crucial platform to build international partnerships and increase awareness of the country’s modernisation efforts: “Expo 2025 offers Tanzania a unique chance to showcase its culture, heritage and natural resources to a global audience, boosting visibility and attracting tourists and investors” ; added that engaging with global businesses at the Expo will help foster trade relationships, promote exports and secure foreign direct investment, benefiting sectors like agriculture, tourism and manufacturing.

a6202.speaker: United Nations World Food Programme (WFP) (statement)
a6202.name: United Nations World Food Programme (WFP) (statement)
a6202.speech: Welcomed a contribution of 23,268 metric tons of rice from the South Korean Ministry of Agriculture, Food and Rural Affairs (MAFRA) valued at US$18 million to support the food needs of refugees in Kenya, according to a statement from the WFP on Friday; the contribution – the largest from South Korea since it began supporting refugees in Kenya in 2018 – will support the food needs of 720,000 refugees in Dadaab and Kakuma refugee camps and Kalobeyei settlement for six months.

a6202.speaker: Baimankay Sankoh, WFP’s Deputy Country Director in Kenya
a6202.name: Baimankay Sankoh
a6202.title: WFP’s Deputy Country Director in Kenya
a6202.speech: “This generous contribution is vital as we work to respond to the needs of an increasing number of refugees in Kenya, while the resources available to support them are decreasing.” ; “Most refugees are unable to work or return home and are entirely dependent on humanitarian assistance to survive. This generous rice contribution from the Republic of Korea is more vital than ever for WFP to continue supporting the food needs of hundreds of thousands of refugees. And we sincerely hope that this expanded rice contribution will continue in the future.”

a6202.speaker: Kang Hyung-shik, Ambassador of South Korea to Kenya
a6202.name: Kang Hyung-shik
a6202.title: Ambassador of South Korea to Kenya
a6202.speech: “The Republic of Korea is proud to stand alongside other nations in responding to the rising hunger crisis and providing hope to thousands of families in the eastern Africa region.” ; “Our history is deeply rooted in global solidarity, and we remain committed to standing with those in need,” the diplomat added.

a6693.speaker: Keir Starmer, British Prime Minister
a6693.name: Keir Starmer
a6693.title: British Prime Minister
a6693.speech: Raised the defence budget, saying he would fund the increase by cutting the overseas development budget from 0.5% of GDP to 0.3%.

a6693.speaker: Humanitarian charities
a6693.name: Humanitarian charities
a6693.speech: Warned it would tarnish British influence abroad and have a devastating impact on those they support.

a6693.speaker: Anneliese Dodds, British international development minister (resignation letter)
a6693.name: Anneliese Dodds
a6693.title: British international development minister (resignation letter)
a6693.speech: Said in a resignation letter to Starmer that the depth of the cuts would make it impossible to maintain Britain's development priorities, including in war-torn Gaza, Sudan and Ukraine ; "Ultimately, these cuts will remove food and healthcare from desperate people - deeply harming the UK's reputation" ; "I know you have been clear that you are not ideologically opposed to international development. But the reality is that this decision is already being portrayed as following in President Trump's slipstream of cuts to USAID" ; told Starmer in the letter she recognised the need to boost defence spending but was disappointed that the aid budget had absorbed the "entire burden" of the decision.

a6693.speaker: Anneliese Dodds, British international development minister
a6693.name: Anneliese Dodds
a6693.title: British international development minister
a6693.speech: Said she had decided to go before the prime minister's trip to Washington but held off making the announcement to avoid overshadowing it.

a6693.speaker: Starmer's spokesman
a6693.name: Starmer's spokesman
a6693.speech: Told reporters he could not immediately comment on Dodds' resignation.

a6693.speaker: OECD data
a6693.name: OECD data
a6693.speech: Britain is the fifth largest international aid donor, giving over $19 billion in 2023, according to OECD data. The United States tops the ranking, followed by Germany, European Union institutions and Japan.

a6899.speaker: Yu Dunhai, Chinese Ambassador to Nigeria
a6899.name: Yu Dunhai
a6899.title: Chinese Ambassador to Nigeria
a6899.speech: Has asked the international community to remain committed to the principles of the United Nations, resist unilateralism, and ensure that “the tragedy of fascism is never repeated” ; He also warned against the rise of historical revisionism and global instability ; “At this critical juncture, it falls upon us to reaffirm our commitment to the international system with the United Nations at its core, the international order based on international law, and the basic norms of international relations embodied in the UN Charter. Together, let us strive to steer the global order toward a future defined by greater fairness, justice, and equality for all.”

a6899.speaker: Yu Dunhai, Chinese Ambassador to Nigeria
a6899.name: Yu Dunhai
a6899.title: Chinese Ambassador to Nigeria
a6899.speech: Described the massacre where Japanese forces brutally killed more than 300,000 civilians and soldiers and committed widespread atrocities as “one of the darkest chapters in modern world history”; said the film served not only as a remembrance but also as a reminder of the dangers of forgetting history ; “In 1931, driven by militarism, Japan launched a brutal war of aggression against China. Then, on December 13, 1937, after capturing the city of Nanjing, Japanese invaders carried out a horrific massacre that lasted six weeks. More than 300,000 Chinese civilians and soldiers were killed—a tragedy now known as the Nanjing Massacre. This remains one of the darkest chapters in modern world history and a profound, enduring sorrow in the hearts of the Chinese people. The film we are about to watch, Dead to Rights, is inspired by these historical events. It offers a unique perspective for reflecting on this period and reminds us of a history we must never forget.”

a6899.speaker: Yu Dunhai, Chinese Ambassador to Nigeria
a6899.name: Yu Dunhai
a6899.title: Chinese Ambassador to Nigeria
a6899.speech: “During the 14 years of resistance, over 35 million Chinese people lost their lives or were injured. China made historic contributions to the victory of the world anti-fascist war and to restoring world peace and order.” ; “During World War II, as the main Eastern theatre in the global fight against fascism, China endured 14 years of relentless resistance. At a staggering cost of more than 35 million military and civilian casualties and direct economic losses exceeding 600 billion US dollars, we dealt a powerful blow to Japanese fascism, crippled Japan’s ambition to expand further, and made historic contributions to restoring world peace and order.”

a6899.speaker: Yu Dunhai, Chinese Ambassador to Nigeria
a6899.name: Yu Dunhai
a6899.title: Chinese Ambassador to Nigeria
a6899.speech: While emphasising that the anniversary was not only about mourning the dead but also about reinforcing commitments to peace, said: “The best way to honour their sacrifice is to cherish peace, protect peace, and strengthen international cooperation.” ; “Today, we gather to commemorate this great victory—to honour history, pay tribute to the fallen, cherish peace, and build a brighter future together. Let history be our guide. Let us preserve, with unwavering resolve, the hard-won outcomes of World War II.”

a7001.speaker: ArcelorMittal (quarterly earnings report)
a7001.name: ArcelorMittal (quarterly earnings report)
a7001.speech: According to the report, the Liberia operation is processing well with production and shipments, supporting the company's ability to deliver higher and more stable profit margins even amid global market pressures ; the global steel giant sees AML's ongoing expansion project, aimed at tripling iron ore production capacity from the current 5 million tonnes to 20 million tonnes per year, as a cornerstone of its investment; the project is reportedly progressing "on time and on budget"; the company anticipates commissioning its full 15Mt concentrator capacity by mid-2025, with a target to reach the full 20Mt run-rate by the end of the year ; the earnings report reaffirmed ArcelorMittal's strategic commitment to Liberia as a key growth frontier, highlighting Liberia alongside major projects in the United States and India as part of its priority investments for 2025.

a7001.speaker: Community leaders and industry observers
a7001.name: Community leaders and industry observers
a7001.speech: Welcomed the decision as a boost to investor confidence and job security.

a7098.speaker: Daniel W. Johannes, President and CEO of the Millennium Challenge Corporation (MCC)
a7098.name: Daniel W. Johannes
a7098.title: President and CEO of the Millennium Challenge Corporation (MCC)
a7098.speech: "Declared that in Benin the MCA had found a good partnership", marking his satisfaction, during his October 2011 visit to Benin a few weeks before the end of the first compact.

a7098.speaker: Samuel Batcho, Coordinator of MCA-Benin
a7098.name: Samuel Batcho
a7098.title: Coordinator of MCA-Benin
a7098.speech: Acknowledged, to national television (ORTB), that the 90 billion invested in the port of Cotonou constitutes "the most important investment the MCA has made in Benin and the second most important in the world".

a7098.speaker: Samuel Batcho, Coordinator of MCA-Benin
a7098.name: Samuel Batcho
a7098.title: Coordinator of MCA-Benin
a7098.speech: Suggested, as for the current state of the port, that "it is a question of the discipline of port actors (freight forwarders, transporters, etc.) that will have to be settled" ; Reported after Saturday's session at the Presidential Palace that "the port must from now on operate in accordance with operating and competitiveness requirements. The MCA authorities' concern is that when the coast guards are in Benin on 6 November 2012, they must be able to decide whether the port complies with ISPS standards (an international security standard)", explaining that if the coast guards find the port non-compliant, ships leaving Cotonou for European and American ports will be subject to "a very rigorous inspection".

a7098.speaker: Michel Raynor, United States Ambassador to Benin
a7098.name: Michel Raynor
a7098.title: United States Ambassador to Benin
a7098.speech: Hammered home, on national television during the port session, that "the durability of the infrastructure built under the MCA is of great concern to the MCA authorities and to the American authorities", adding that it is a matter of the port's compliance with international standards, notably security and competitiveness.

a7098.speaker: Boni Yayi, President of Benin
a7098.name: Boni Yayi
a7098.title: President of Benin
a7098.speech: Reassured during the session held at the port of Cotonou: "We are going to take steps for the future and organise ourselves better. The investments will be made sustainable," before committing to take the file "personally in hand".

a7194.speaker: White House official (anonymous), told CNN
a7194.name: White House official (anonymous)
a7194.title: told CNN
a7194.speech: A White House official told CNN that the meeting is intended to “explore commercial opportunities that benefit both the American people and our African partners.”

a7194.speaker: Professor Christopher Afoke Isike, African international relations scholar at the University of Pretoria
a7194.name: Professor Christopher Afoke Isike
a7194.title: African international relations scholar at the University of Pretoria
a7194.speech: “This is not engagement - it's cherry-picking,” said Professor Christopher Afoke Isike. “Trump is targeting countries that are either politically pliable or rich in resources, and avoiding those that assert themselves independently or align with powers like China or Russia.”

a7194.speaker: Mamadou Thior, Dakar-based journalist who covered the first US-Africa Leaders' Summit in 2014
a7194.name: Mamadou Thior
a7194.title: Dakar-based journalist who covered the first US-Africa Leaders' Summit in 2014
a7194.speech: said the nature of Trump's engagement is unmistakable: “Trump is not looking for partners - he's looking for deals. And only with countries he believes he can control.”

a7194.speaker: Lilongwe-based political analyst (anonymous, requested anonymity)
a7194.name: Lilongwe-based political analyst (anonymous
a7194.title: requested anonymity)
a7194.speech: “This kind of exclusion should be a wake-up call,” said a Lilongwe-based political analyst. “If Malawi wants to be taken seriously, it needs to do more than just show up at donor forums. It needs a clear, assertive strategy on global partnerships, trade, and diplomacy.”

a7346.speaker: Ron DeSantis, Governor of Florida
a7346.name: Ron DeSantis
a7346.title: Governor of Florida
a7346.speech: said on Friday at a briefing that during a 72-hour period this week the Florida Department of Transportation removed 2,200 truckloads of debris – more than 40,000 cubic yards – from Pinellas County barrier islands near the mouth of Tampa Bay ; “I don’t think there’s ever been that much debris removed in such a short period of time.”

a7346.speaker: PowerOutage.us (website)
a7346.name: PowerOutage.us (website)
a7346.speech: According to the website, the number of Florida homes and businesses without electricity dropped to about 2.27 million by late Friday morning, from a high of more than 3.4 million in Milton’s immediate aftermath.

a7346.speaker: Major General John Haas, the governor’s senior military advisor
a7346.name: Major General John Haas
a7346.title: the governor’s senior military advisor
a7346.speech: said more than 6,500 National Guard members have been activated in 23 Florida counties, and are involved with search and rescue, ground and air reconnaissance, humanitarian assistance, route clearance and other efforts.

a7346.speaker: Kenneth Welch, Mayor of St. Petersburg
a7346.name: Kenneth Welch
a7346.title: Mayor of St. Petersburg
a7346.speech: said at a news briefing that in St. Petersburg hundreds of trees were downed, and more than 100 traffic signals were not working as of late Thursday.

a7346.speaker: Adrian Petrila, Mayor of St. Pete Beach
a7346.name: Adrian Petrila
a7346.title: Mayor of St. Pete Beach
a7346.speech: told ABC News that clearing debris from the twin storms will take weeks ; “It’s going to be a very long time for us,” he said, adding that most of the city’s houses were uninhabitable with no sewer or water service.

a7346.speaker: C.K. Moore, emergency-management official, Hillsborough County
a7346.name: C.K. Moore
a7346.title: emergency-management official, Hillsborough County
a7346.speech: said workers have visited more than 450 homes and businesses to assess damage since Thursday, and that there were 13 structures known to be destroyed and another 111 with major damage.

a7346.speaker: C.K. Moore, emergency-management official, Hillsborough County
a7346.name: C.K. Moore
a7346.title: emergency-management official, Hillsborough County
a7346.speech: said that unlike Helene, whose storm surge caused most of its damage along the coast, Milton’s strong winds and extreme rainfall created problems across the county, with Plant City, more than 20 miles (32 km) inland, experiencing major flooding.

a7346.speaker: C.K. Moore, emergency-management official, Hillsborough County
a7346.name: C.K. Moore
a7346.title: emergency-management official, Hillsborough County
a7346.speech: “We’re just hoping for a period of calm so we can clean this stuff up and give residents a sense of normalcy.”

a7346.speaker: Adam Smith, communications director, city of Tampa
a7346.name: Adam Smith
a7346.title: communications director, city of Tampa
a7346.speech: said the city of Tampa does not yet know the costs associated with storm cleanup, and that the work will likely require months of clearing downed trees and vegetation on top of removing household debris left from Helene, which is the city’s first priority.

a7346.speaker: Office of Governor Ron DeSantis
a7346.name: Office of Governor Ron DeSantis
a7346.speech: According to DeSantis’ office, nearly 1,200 people have been rescued since Milton made landfall on Wednesday evening.

a7346.speaker: The White House
a7346.name: The White House
a7346.speech: said President Joe Biden will visit Florida on Sunday to survey the damage.

a7346.speaker: The White House
a7346.name: The White House
a7346.speech: pledged government support as the full extent of the damage was still being surveyed.

a7346.speaker: Marcos Alvarez, Morningstar DBRS analyst
a7346.name: Marcos Alvarez
a7346.title: Morningstar DBRS analyst
a7346.speech: said on Friday that Milton, the fifth-most-intense Atlantic hurricane on record, could cost insurers between $30 billion and $60 billion – a projection lower than the up to $100 billion estimated by the firm before the storm’s arrival.

a7346.speaker: The Biden administration
a7346.name: The Biden administration
a7346.speech: said the Federal Emergency Management Agency would need additional funding from Congress, where the Republicans control the House and Democrats control the Senate, and urged lawmakers, who are on recess, to act.

a7346.speaker: Florida Department of Law Enforcement (cited by CBS News)
a7346.name: Florida Department of Law Enforcement (cited by CBS News)
a7346.speech: There were at least 16 hurricane-related deaths, CBS News cited the Florida Department of Law Enforcement as saying.

a7346.speaker: Local officials in St. Lucie County
a7346.name: Local officials in St. Lucie County
a7346.speech: According to local officials, a flurry of tornadoes killed several people in St. Lucie County, including at least two in a senior-living community.

a7346.speaker: National Hurricane Center (preliminary analysis)
a7346.name: National Hurricane Center (preliminary analysis)
a7346.speech: According to a preliminary analysis posted by the National Hurricane Center, between Siesta Key and Fort Myers Beach peak water levels reached five to 10 feet (1.5 to three m) above ground level.

a7377.speaker: National Empowerment of Positive Women United (NEPWU)
a7377.name: National Empowerment of Positive Women United (NEPWU)
a7377.speech: Reveals that around 70,000 people have been directly affected by Donald Trump's 90-day suspension of U.S. foreign aid.

a7377.speaker: Mama Evelyn Letio, NEPWU Executive Director
a7377.name: Mama Evelyn Letio
a7377.title: NEPWU Executive Director
a7377.speech: Addressing a press conference on February 17, said the PEPFAR program used to donate $1 million annually to the organization and accounted for 75% of the organization's budget; revealed that within an estimated number of nearly 200,000 people living with HIV in South Sudan, nearly 70,000 rely on international assistance; said the suspension threatens to reverse years of momentum gained in fighting the pandemic. ; "The abrupt halt in funding jeopardizes these essential services, threatens to reverse years of progress made in the fight against HIV epidemic, and potentially leading to disruption of access to life-saving medications." ; Stated that the situation could lead to potential health crises for those dependent on continuous treatment; narrated that inconsistent use of antiretroviral (ARVs) drugs can result in drug resistance and therefore increase new HIV infections and transmissions, as well as Tuberculosis and other sexually transmitted infections. ; "It also poses threats to prevention processes including awareness campaigns, condom distribution, access to pre-exposure prophylaxis and post-exposure prophylaxis to the key and vulnerable population, such as IDPs, refugees, and sex workers, among others." ; Fears that scaling back relief funding for combating HIV will likely result in higher rates of new infections in the country.

a7377.speaker: Mama Evelyn Letio, NEPWU Executive Director
a7377.name: Mama Evelyn Letio
a7377.title: NEPWU Executive Director
a7377.speech: Revealed that medical supplies for people living with the virus are generally provided by the global fund through the UN Development Agency UNDP; noted that Washington's stop work order has severely affected community components responsible for counselling, the monitoring of viral load and the distribution of drugs. ; "There are those who are supposed to be refilled after three months or after six months. But because of this freeze, the volunteers are not able to round them up to check who still has the drugs, who doesn't have." ; "And we also have community-based HIV testing services, which has been interrupted. The index testing within a family, children that are born, we need to continuously keep testing the family who have accepted." ; "The viral load sample collection, every six months they have to take my blood to see; is the virus decreasing or increasing? We need to enhance adherence counseling to this person with the high viral load. Right now it is not taking place because of this stop work order."

a7377.speaker: Mama Evelyn Letio, NEPWU Executive Director
a7377.name: Mama Evelyn Letio
a7377.title: NEPWU Executive Director
a7377.speech: Revealed that about 2,800 children will miss school due to the freeze; said these are children who lost their parents due to HIV/AIDS and the U.S. grant has been instrumental in helping to pay for their school fees, and that these children are likely to miss school this year due to the freeze.

a7377.speaker: Margret Jokudu, 30-year-old mother of four, mentor mother at Juba Teaching Hospital and NEPWU employee
a7377.name: Margret Jokudu
a7377.title: 30-year-old mother of four, mentor mother at Juba Teaching Hospital and NEPWU employee
a7377.speech: Said the little incentive she used to earn helps provide for her family including paying school fees, and is now afraid that the freeze is going to prevent them from sending their children to school. ; "We are positive, but we are producing negative children, and they are living healthy, and we are caring for them. And the little money we are getting, the funding, it helps us to pay them to school." ; "Some of us are widows. This money is like our husband, helping us to pay children at school, feeding them, everything, even renting. But now it is stopped. It means that our life is now very, very, very hard."

a7377.speaker: Abala Victor, 42-year-old father of two who lost his job
a7377.name: Abala Victor
a7377.title: 42-year-old father of two who lost his job
a7377.speech: Fears the funding pause might deny them life-saving drugs and lead to their death: "It is going to happen because I am not able to reach the hospital. Maybe even if the drug stops from the hospital, which means all of us who are positive, we are going to die."

a7377.speaker: Angelina Doki, 45-year-old mother of three
a7377.name: Angelina Doki
a7377.title: 45-year-old mother of three
a7377.speech: Said she fears thousands of people living with the virus might not be able to receive ARVs due to the stop work order: "It has affected us because the drugs are not going to reach to those who are still in rural areas. Leave us in Juba town. There are some rural areas. The state there, this thing is going to affect them. It affected us here, it will also affect them there."

a7377.speaker: Medecins Sans Frontieres (MSF)
a7377.name: Medecins Sans Frontieres (MSF)
a7377.speech: On February 13 said the U.S. decision to temporarily freeze funding to PEPFAR alongside all other foreign aid for at least a 90-day period has had immediate effects on people living with HIV; said that although the US has since clarified that certain treatment programs can continue at least until April, it is concerned that critical elements of the PEPFAR program remain frozen; calls on the US government to immediately resume funding for the full range of PEPFAR operations as well as other critical health and humanitarian aid; said a limited waiver issued by Washington on 1st February for the resumption of some programming with specific guidance for HIV remains unclear, and it did not immediately reach PEPFAR country teams.

a7377.speaker: Avril Benoit, chief executive officer of MSF USA
a7377.name: Avril Benoit
a7377.title: chief executive officer of MSF USA
a7377.speech: "More than three weeks since the US government froze PEPFAR funding, there is still widespread confusion and uncertainty as to whether this critical lifeline for millions of people has been cut off." ; "Despite a limited waiver covering some activities, what our teams are seeing in many of the countries where we work is that people have already lost access to lifesaving care and have no idea whether or when their treatment will continue."
